[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144005840/662105059/1231236074?refcode=RS_EM_FR_2026.11.24_OliviaTopper&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NzI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NTEyYTcwYi02NGU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=W3tNvSz361Gou-K9muOxn3-1SWLcGMVcuct8tvnizfw=&emci=b7aa57a3-38e8-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=7512a70b-64e8-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=23483442) | Peter, _I wanted to follow up on the email I sent you about my sister Olivia._ When I told you her story, I talked about how much Medicaid meant to our family. How it helped us get Olivia the care and support she needed. And how growing up with her shaped the work I do every single day in Congress. **I also told you we needed to flip the House to protect families like mine — _and we did._** We won the House and the Senate. And in January, we will take control of both chambers of Congress. There’s so much we need to get to work on: rolling back the Medicaid cuts, supporting caregivers and health care providers, and making sure EVERYONE can count on the care they need when and where they need it. It’s way past time for universal health care!! I know we won't fix everything overnight — but starting in January, we'll have a real chance to make things better for families like mine. And I plan to make the most of it. I’ll be thinking about Olivia every step of the way. — Emily 💙 If you believe you received this message in error or wish to no longer receive email from us, please [unsubscribe](https://secure.ngpvan.com/p/c9SZbdkbdUi3uhuNc8iU_A2?unsubscribedata=vSVihN71OzmBuRcvEYNKW1R%2BkYAuIzSwlzDI6ybZon78Tb%2B367r1%2B%2Fcym7mYQ%2F45%2BGnOJRynuj2TKfiAa8i5h02vnBBQ91RFQ5oiQec%2FDM7ggXn2AKhhHP5C7BIhsIzrfVWgguruFF%2FgIVWM%2F%2BpwGeECgSJkty2vUC5yLBpuxyojTeUxUjXBfChVXULyMugEn1mCE7EeWsekbtWAhDPBSq%2FsWd6MCRtpDcQiAReKNW3A36q3u5riqyi9h%2F%2FvfxFQDvCQpnRZh0TOmECq8BaEfUcqmHk4oFGZrsm7K7ox8IvbE2GijfCtsugPDBgvN%2BoKVnu9x%2FggQu7z4IZ0N1W1SHwbTaMAlMVgUE2%2Flrb17hAX8AWCweC25Nvm7EXczA1cQMsT%2B1dMlFeZEH721rzTKoljZPGzDJezyB03pDLJCbSsbpGF44iiK9zi8WEgrzgk). —- FORWARD —- Hey, Peter, I want to get a little personal. I’m going to talk to you about my sister Olivia, because Olivia’s story is such an important part of the work I do. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144005841/662105060/38395969?refcode=RS_EM_FR_2026.11.24_OliviaTopper&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NzI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NTEyYTcwYi02NGU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=W3tNvSz361Gou-K9muOxn3-1SWLcGMVcuct8tvnizfw=) Olivia was born with microcephaly, which meant her head and brain were smaller than expected. From the very beginning, she needed complex medical care, surgeries, and equipment — a wheelchair, feeding pumps, a nebulizer, and more. While my dad’s Union job provided health insurance — it didn’t cover everything Olivia needed. **Medicaid helped fill that gap and made it possible for our family to give Olivia the care she deserved** — from medical equipment and appointments at Mary Bridge and Tacoma General to home visits from early intervention specialists, nurses, and therapists. _I learned at a young age that the decisions lawmakers make can have a profound impact on whether families like mine can get the care they need._ Today, I fight to protect Medicaid because I know firsthand what it can mean for a family. The Republican controlled Congress is putting that care at risk, and we have to make sure families don’t lose access to the programs they rely on. ## Horrible Bosses, Huang Edition
Imagine sitting in a meeting with your boss and your colleagues. Your boss, in a towering fit of rage and with all the solemnity of the Pope, announces that he intends to kill you.
He threatens to tear the arms from another employee and use the bloody appendages to beat you to death. He promises to scalp a third colleague and urinate upon the exposed brain. Then, turning to an elderly employee in his seventies, the boss announces that you and everyone else in the company would like to see the old fellow dead.
One might expect that such a workplace nightmare would earn the perpetrator a psychiatric evaluation, a security escort, and perhaps a permanent vacation from corporate management.
But this is no longer the sort of thing that ends a CEO's career in modern American capitalism under Donald Trump.
According to reporting by _The New York Times_ , Nvidia employees have allegedly endured precisely this sort of extraordinary verbal savagery at the hands of their chief executive, Jensen Huang.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a1edebb6-db7f-4046-a0dc-ae89f2a9ec14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
If the accounts are accurate, the atmosphere in certain corporate meetings would appear to have been less reminiscent of a boardroom than of a particularly horrific chapter in the history of the Mafia.
And the allegations do not stop there.

No president is above the law. And Trump’s connections to Epstein raise serious questions.

👉 Donald Trump’s name appears throughout those files — along with records of his past relationship with Epstein.
_**👉**_ And yet the Trump administration has spent years trying to slow-walk transparency and avoid real accountability.
_**In fact, he's even threatened to prosecute me. **_
That’s not how oversight works. Congress has the authority — and the responsibility — to investigate misconduct, demand documents, and require testimony under oath to write laws preventing these horrible abuses from happening again.

| | | | Peter, The results of our race are final, and voters have reelected Michael Baumgartner to represent Eastern Washington in Congress. This isn't the result we worked so hard for. subject: Learn to Be - a worthy cause

body:
#
Six years ago during COVID, my campaign launched a free volunteer tutoring program for kids called Homework Helpers.
Tons of people signed up to be trained and vetted to provide free Zoom tutoring to kids and families.
I volunteered as a tutor as well.
Over the years, the effort has grown so much that we had to partner with Learn to Be -- and today we are celebrating 500,000 HOURS OF FREE TUTORING to more than 20,000 students since it launched.
But many more need our help, and that is why I am writing today.
Learn to Be is a non-profit that focuses on underserved communities. Students get to work with the same tutor until they reach their goals and are often assigned a tutor within a day of signing up. They also offer tutoring in English and Spanish.
[This holiday season, if you can, please consider offering either your time as a tutor or a small donation to help the next 500,000 hours of free tutoring for kids and families. ](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/39655?t=3&akid=12520%2E2526796%2EQauylK)
**[https://www.learntobe.org/donate](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/39655?t=4&akid=12520%2E2526796%2EQauylK)**
Thank you,
Alexandria

But many more need our help, and that is why I am writing today. Learn to Be is a non-profit that focuses on underserved communities. Students get to work with the same tutor until they reach their goals and are often assigned a tutor within a day of signing up. They also offer tutoring in English and Spanish. Thank you, Alexandria Here's a photo from a Learn to Be event in the Bronx. | ---|--- | | | ---|---|---|--- Email us: mailto: speak@ocasiocortez.com

Years ago, when we founded this organization, we weren’t sure where we would end up.
#

Friend,
Before the Thanksgiving holiday, I wanted to express my gratitude.
Years ago, when we founded this organization, we weren’t sure where we would end up. Most people thought taking on the NRA was madness, and were happy to tell me so.
What I did know is that many people felt the same way I did: That the rising tide of gun violence was a crisis, and that our children were worth fighting for. What I needed was for those people to be courageous enough to do something about it.
This work never gets easier. Every life lost to gun violence is an unimaginable tragedy. But the weight gets lighter as more and more people take that courageous step and join us. And today, we have built a nationwide team. We have elected champions in state legislatures, in governors offices, and in Washington. We have a track record of passing life saving regulations.
Thank you. After all that, I shouldn’t need to ask you for more. It should be enough. But today, even after our victories, gun violence is the number one cause of death for American children and teenagers.
As long as American kids are being needlessly killed by guns, I can’t quit. As long as there is work for us to do, I will not quit.
And with an incredibly important decision on assault weapons bans ahead of the Supreme Court next month, I need to ask you:

subject: Tell Congress: Don't make hunger worse
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Our Revolution click here to unsubscribe
body:
[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

As people across the country prepare to gather around the table for
Thanksgiving, for millions of families, the question isn't what's on the
menu. It's whether they'll have enough food to get through the week.

More than 5 million people have already lost access to SNAP since
Republicans passed their Big Brutal Bill last July. And the damage isn't
over.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40181?source=email-20261125&t=1011&akid=11632%2E5885482%2Ed_CSgC ]Headline: The astonishing toll of America’s food stamp cuts.
Subheadline: Millions of children will go hungry if Congress doesn’t act
soon.

That same law is shifting more of SNAP's costs onto states, which are now
being forced to confront a devastating choice: absorb these new costs, cut
other essential services, or potentially leave SNAP altogether.

That means even more children, older adults, veterans, and people with
disabilities could lose access to the food assistance they count on.
Congress has one more chance to stop this before the year is over.

As lawmakers negotiate must-pass spending legislation, they must protect
SNAP by eliminating the new requirement that states pay a share of benefit
costs.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40181?source=email-20261125&t=1012&akid=11632%2E5885482%2Ed_CSgC ]Will you send a message to your representative and senators right now,
urging them to protect SNAP NOW, before even more people are forced to go
hungry?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40181?source=email-20261125&t=1013&akid=11632%2E5885482%2Ed_CSgC ]ADD YOUR NAME

Thanksgiving is supposed to be a time when we come together, share a meal,
and make sure no one is left out. But while families are doing everything
they can to stretch their grocery budgets, politicians in Washington are
making it harder for millions of people to afford food.

SNAP is one of the most effective tools we have to fight hunger and help
families make ends meet. States shouldn't be forced to choose between
keeping people fed and funding other essential services — and families
shouldn't pay the price for decisions made in Washington.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40181?source=email-20261125&t=1014&akid=11632%2E5885482%2Ed_CSgC ]Headline: ‘Treat This Like the Emergency It Is’: Dems Urged to Act
Swiftly to Undo Trump-GOP Assault on Food Aid

Congress needs to hear from us before it leaves for the year. Our
Revolution is mobilizing people across the country to demand that
lawmakers protect SNAP and reverse the damage of last year's cuts.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40181?source=email-20261125&t=1015&akid=11632%2E5885482%2Ed_CSgC ]This Thanksgiving, let's make sure Congress hears one clear message:
don't make hunger worse. Add your name and demand SNAP protections in the
year-end spending package.

| | | Fellow Conservative, Let me be blunt.

For weeks before Election Day, I warned that we could lose Texas. Not just the Senate race. Every single statewide race. **Far too few believed it was possible. Then it happened.**

2026 was not simply a blue wave. It was a blue tsunami. We lost the United States House. We lost the United States Senate. We lost in historically red states like Kansas, South Carolina, Ohio, and Iowa. And in Texas, we lost every single statewide election and the Texas State House.

Sometimes history is to be celebrated. Other times, it is to be mourned. But always, it must be reckoned with.

Here is the hard truth. Our voters showed up. Republicans, Libertarians and Independents went to the polls, and too many of them rejected our candidates. Families were hurting from high prices, and elected Republicans didn't do enough to address their very real pain.

A Republic survives on the truth. Dictatorships survive on lies. So today, I'm asking YOU to give it to me straight.

body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=56%2E6803%2EY1S9AP)
[](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261125.NUydda&refcode=em20261125-56&t=3&akid=56%2E6803%2EY1S9AP)
I felt optimistic heading into Election Day, but I didn't dare imagine the results would be this broad. I'm so proud of the American people for paying attention and showing out to bring the biggest wave of climate champions to all levels of government.
But as you know, winning elections is just the first step. **What follows is where the real work begins.**
People voted for so much more than the other guy this year. We voted to love one another. For our movement, that means:
* **Blocking what’s bad:** Holding the line against the Trump administration, fighting creeping authoritarianism, and stopping the fossil fuel industry and AI developers from buying our government.
* **Fighting for what’s good:** Putting power directly into the hands of working people, lowering utility bills, and fighting for a liveable future for everyone who calls this beautiful country home.

**[That work doesn’t just happen overnight. In fact, JanePAC has been investing in states like Arizona and Pennsylvania year after year to finally take back the legislature. Sometimes change takes time, and it always takes a whole lot of people. It dies quietly, when Democrats assume the fight is over and stop showing up for the races that are still left.
This is Rep. Patricia "Pat" Moore (D-LA). On November 3, I finished ahead of my MAGA opponent in Louisiana's 5th District and forced a December 12 runoff.
For one incredible week, Democrats from across the country rallied behind us. We raised more than $1 million. I was overwhelmed by the support.
**_Then it stopped._**
With the big win on November 3 making folks comfortable, no national attention on our race, and Thanksgiving around the corner, our fundraising has nosedived. Take a look:
[](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Sb6jWVItwm4BMjXtLAFQo3t7uNnsdxs6KfpYsgY-ci30L6GPvDJRRvLBELTkUFIQ65YWf2zG6hqoPTw51AXci4G3wE56KBTb3VrShmxvB_qunPTKUAAEJEtFckATCeffzp44mwinysmj_WKrW09Fl3S8D256xeXDAcWKzJXWR61RGkFgZiVpOL_R1xGFdrJGhhIsWq7k7HWs0Vzmj6jBV4cmFX-xq9BOGTynicIfy_HQlzDU2Hpcjg==&c=1aLc1hRse6Dt6bS0ns5SYH3N9atE_lK9GYwQHb_m1Rt5wtm1m7qNRg==&ch=DLmBJcI1VPv04iF7qVOQlcSFXQFt1emh8N5n8HwrzB4cMiz4BjFFxQ==)

I'm 17 days away from becoming the first Black woman Louisiana has EVER sent to Congress. I'm outnumbered and outgunned, deep in MAGA territory, with very little support from Washington. And the only thing that can carry us over the finish line is you.

name: Defenders of Wildlife
subject: What is a Chinook salmon?
body:
If you think your trip home is stressful...
If you think your trip home is stressful...
| [](https://support.defenders.org/s/6361011/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
|
---
[](https://support.defenders.org/s/6361012/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_What’s a Chinook salmon?_**
A long journey home against harrowing odds, all for the sake of family. Maybe this sounds like your travel plan this week, but it’s also true for Chinook salmon! These remarkable fish spend years in the sea before beginning their legendary migrations from the ocean to the home rivers where they were born!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Where can they be found?_**
Chinook salmon range from California to Alaska, and even as far across the Pacific as Northern Japan. The important question isn’t so much where they can be found as where they’re missing: While many populations are healthy and plentiful, Chinook salmon in the Northwest have been decimated by dams on the rivers they call home!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Okay, so?_**
As many of us are working up an appetite for a feast, the Salish sea is full of some very hungry orcas. Southern Resident orcas depend on Chinook salmon for survival. Their fates are tied together, and it’s up to us to stop these species from disappearing!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_How can I help?_**
The good news is there’s a plan to end the salmon famine! We’re working with regional leaders to restore the river systems that salmon and orcas both depend on for survival. Your support will help us bring back the bounty of salmon to the Northwest!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
|
---

name: Wes Moore
subject: What I’m feeling thankful for
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2335%2E1086043%2E7Rvupu)
Peter, this week, I’m feeling thankful.
Thankful for God’s grace and another year of life.
Thankful for Dawn, our kids, and Tucker.
Thankful for a week full of friends, family, turkey, and the Ravens.
Thankful for four more years to serve the people of Maryland.
None of that is lost on me. I grew up as the son of an immigrant single mother. I didn’t come from money or prestige. I came from hard work, community, and people who refused to give up on me.
So this week, I’m thinking about everyone who stood with me along the way, and about the Maryland families who still need someone in their corner.
You’re one of those people who stood with me.
Whether you donated, talked to a friend, or simply shared our story, you helped make these four more years possible.
Thank you, and a happy early Thanksgiving.
-- Wes Moore

I served in the U.S. Army as a Ranger, a Green Beret, and a Delta Force operator.

Today I lead Rescue in Blue, and the mission of our organization is to train and equip local law enforcement — at home and internationally — to recognize trafficking, arrest predators, and rescue victims.

I want to tell you about a girl who was just 13 years old.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNzEsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABFHGpM-siVqYtBkNjr3NvzTxlKv3y3ayQYnnrWUZrF4jOdx1VSwOyz4EQIrdylz9DpP2ntzX-XVjFZTpdnV_7Z4pY8Z1LiPyVx8UjDD8

Home should have been the safest place in her world.

It wasn’t.

After she was sexually abused by a father figure, she ran away.

She was a child looking for safety. For belonging. For someone who would make her feel wanted.

Instead, she ended up alone on the streets of Atlanta… and someone noticed.

It started with attention. Then acceptance. Then the promise of a “family.”

Slowly, that attention became control. What looked like protection became exploitation.

She was trafficked.

Years went by.

The little girl who ran from home became a young mother herself.

And now she was fighting for two.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNzEsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABFHGpM-trWu2gSR87oB0bSjIfikRgh2LrAaU8Z0b8whXkvXIR07yWr00Ywa4xYcfWgyaQNfHiNa_MOb_v37DDE55TpcUFfkioZB-cJJE
Join the Rescue

With a one-year-old baby in her arms, she made a brave choice.

She ran from the people who had controlled her for years.

She knew how dangerous it was. But she would not let her daughter live the life she had lived.

She needed more than a way out.

She needed a safe place to go and people willing to stand beside her.

That’s where Rescue in Blue stepped in.

We helped get mother and daughter to safety and connected them with a recovery program where healing could begin.

And we worked alongside law enforcement to bring her story to investigators — giving them a chance to hold her trafficker accountable and find other girls who may still be under his control.

For the first time, this young mom had people protecting her instead of using her.

And her little girl has a chance to grow up safe.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNzEsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABFHGpM-u4Qqt2jgqU6jgrW46RrV3YPeNa9KQrK4T53ZwpYAdIiCsyASZE80uCXKCKLBUABKBRE1BVMv6B_eZ6_rPLadKxt3Ey2gPbuhj
Join the Rescue

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNzEsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABFHGpM-vxgVFkYXyzYMDl6X4iwCA70-I5U1kkuQkc-cgOrHRF5ZdtKSxO3dZF38lJbKLDMM0Qgf93fgiRV73Reby4kpdLlcZM7ESuWu7

Friend, here’s what most people don’t know.

Every day, police officers come face to face with trafficking victims. On traffic stops. Hotel checks. Domestic calls.

But most officers have never been trained to recognize trafficking.

So they don’t know what they’re looking at.

A scared teenager becomes “a runaway.” A victim becomes “a problem.” And the trafficker keeps working.

That’s the gap Rescue in Blue closes.

We give officers two days of hands-on training with tools most departments can’t afford. They learn how traffickers think, how buyers operate, and how to build cases that hold up in court.

Then we go into the field with them for a live operation to find victims, arrest predators, and bring children home.

Over a career, one officer may answer thousands of calls.

When that officer knows the signs, any one of those calls could be the moment a child is seen and set free.

As a Green Beret, I lived by the words “free the oppressed.” In Delta Force, it was “oppressors beware.”

At Rescue in Blue, we live by both.

## Family Surrounded by Gators Rescued
Volusia County deputies used a raft Monday to pull a family, including a 6-month-old baby and an 8-year-old who uses a wheelchair, from a [flooded Stone Island home](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkDGypCAQQE-DGRa0yGhAsInZbLqh1UIzsoUyBYzW3H7L_fNP8NN-1V393p_7fMcQw_74jRsZn_y801ki1Up5Lq-c02t35DxuIb4zFfsiV9MMAjSXkkM_o63hoFlh48xNDSiWhoy8jb0WCgQ0qxk8yIW0IguLG1Ar1E6PVjiBrlNSN8Fc96SEXoped2M7LiMob2H0w9CBFkwJcqGm3P5NYffxnQ7KPqYcHLY2bU00a63PwrpfDCYG03mebdn3elyUwXRJXWOsduWfRf4lxT9W3Oe0XSw5chwzIcfCMcbwwJpy4d81-Jo2YjA12bjnGWIMRd-YEo8NQ_z_Tf1hyMPAvwAAAP__NTSLTw) as rising water and multiple alligators surrounded the house. [Body-camera video](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJyk0b-Oo0AMBvCngc7R4BD-FBTXpNtrr0SG8QTfGhzNDEG8_Sm79wZbWZblT_rp-_MxfpCobI_ftPIQLIwbH0k5Z45j2mO0ffPsA62iZ-Q07-yzjeiwgaoCvI00Z3nxWFPph7buyE0lD1Xb3xpXo8NyGWr0FQcXuJl9IMSpxdCGq-v6KXTTzZUyvPOqCm-VuzXX_tJPPdZhxj503RUbV9SOvWSLl78mW9DTXhyDWhRPl9nWUocl52cqrr8KvBd4_6S8vw8F3t-e96AstsFhUX2B9__P4Pm5Z-EE3zb4hkKItkJQM39Q5piAEpCqPChbTKB7_ISNKU4nNLDalhcw9TDRdEIHJ1P82r0kmpQ9zIuoh2Nh1nkhiRDMvGwPKOPgn4eoSmraonaPlUS_SPmHbbwG_BcAAP__t8WlDQ) shows a deputy wading through the water and asking, _"There's alligators out there_?" clean_body: FEMA approved on Monday to reimburse Hurricane Helene repairs and fund future disaster protection. | | | | | | Wednesday, November 25, 2026 ---|--- Good Morning! On this day in 1838, of federal troops executed Tsali, a Cherokee man who had fled removal and hid in the Smoky Mountains near present-day Bryson City, after soldiers were killed during his family’s escape. His story later inspired the long-running outdoor drama Unto These Hills. Drought is that once existed but are now submerged by Jordan Lake. Learn more in Top Stories. How long is that turkey actually safe in your fridge? About 48 million Americans get food poisoning every year, and no week fills more refrigerators with risky leftovers than this one. Today, we're breaking down seven kitchen rules from the CDC and USDA that keep Thanksgiving leftovers from sending you to the hospital. Does the sniff test really work? And why does washing your chicken spread germs across the whole kitchen? Check out The Flyover Podcast to hear the one rule that could save your life. ! I don’t know if you remember this one, but back in April we featured Montgomery Ward in our Sunday Whatever Happened To? section. We mentioned that you could still shop Wards online, and we loved hearing from readers who grew up flipping through the catalog. A few of you even wrote in to say you used to work there. So here’s a fun full-circle moment for Thanksgiving week. Today’s sponsor is Montgomery Ward. If you’re looking to cross a few names off your Christmas list before Thursday, . The bulk, more than $178 million, flows through FEMA’s Public Assistance program. The largest share goes to North Carolina Emergency Management ($103.3 million) and NCDOT ($62.5 million) for bridge and road work across Western North Carolina. Smaller awards : $6.1 million for Asheville Christian Academy, $1.4 million for road-culvert repairs in Montreat, and $1.2 million for Ashe County’s Riverview Community Center. Another $8.3 million comes through the , meant to reduce damage from future disasters. Since 2024, FEMA says it has obligated more than $7.5 billion for Helene and other North Carolina disasters. Stein Announces $37.8M for Mountain Districts Gov. Josh Stein Monday to rebuild storm-battered commercial districts in six Western North Carolina towns, two years after Hurricane Helene. The money, awarded through the state’s Renew NC program from a , funds downtown projects in Lansing, Marshall, Hot Springs, Buncombe County, Lake Junaluska, and Morganton. Marshall’s historic courthouse and Buncombe County’s Swannanoa corridor drew the largest shares, with $10 million each. Stein, a Democrat, made the alongside Republican Sen. Ted Budd and Democrat Sen.-elect Roy Cooper, who toured the region as governor after the storm. Officials said 74% of Helene-damaged public roads and bridges have been restored, and the last closed stretch of the Blue Ridge Parkway reopened over the weekend. A second round of nearly $74 million is expected in December. Drought Exposes Jordan Lake’s Lost Towns A prolonged drought has dropped Jordan Lake low enough to expose the that stood in Chatham County’s New Hope River Valley before the reservoir swallowed them. Off a gravel lot on Farrington Road, receding water has uncovered traces of Seaforth, Pea Ridge, and Farrington: wooden railroad planks, building foundations, and what looks like an old main street. Some of the infrastructure , local historian Heather Leah said after touring the site. She described a string of small farming settlements that most lake visitors never knew existed. "Thousands of people go boating and hiking all around Jordan Lake every year, and many people have no idea that there’s an entire lost community under the lake," Leah said. | Flying together with our sponsor Remember the Montgomery Ward Christmas Wish List? Think cozy pajamas for Christmas morning, a new cookware set for the family cook, and toys for the grandkids. Wards even sorts gifts by price, so it’s easy to start with gifts under $25 or $50. A few down-ballot races, including a Greensboro-area state House recount, remain pending. () ➤ I-77: The revived I-77 South toll lane project could stretch 3 miles past the state line into York County, South Carolina, potentially reaching Gold Hill Road in Fort Mill. The plan would need both Carolinas to agree on toll costs and collection. () ➤Mecklenburg County: Prosecutors dismissed, with prejudice, a felony charge against Democratic Rep.-elect LaKesha Womack over an overdue 2019 car rental, after she paid the company and it declined to pursue prosecution. () ➤ RDU Airport: Raleigh-Durham International Airport is adding 2,600 parking spaces in its Economy 3 lot this holiday season, bringing the lot to 6,400 spots. It’s part of a $2.5 billion expansion that will eventually grow Economy 3 from 3,800 spaces to nearly 11,000. () ➤ Outer Banks: NC State researchers launched an online fair sharing more than two years of Hatteras and Ocracoke coastal flooding findings, including interactive maps and surveys for eight communities, after storms twice canceled in-person events. () ➤ Charlotte: The 80th annual Novant Health Thanksgiving Parade, set for Wednesday in Uptown, was called off after organizers cited forecasted high winds, rain, and cold. Charlotte Center City Partners said ticket holders will get automatic refunds. () ➤ Cary: Science teacher Kathy Cargill was one of 24 home bakers featured on the 2026 Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic , the CBS holiday special hosted by Drew Barrymore that aired Monday night. ## Broderick Officially Wins 4th District
Democrat Victoria Broderick [won Tennessee's 4th Congressional District](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkDHO3CAUhE-DO1aAAZuCIo27P21Ki4Xn9VMwWPBkZ28fbaTkAqlHmpnv-_G1fgXMWF7fwwGeaFsL3D0DEbRV056wU8NIN5YCLdayYTtgVUJZLiVXZg2R8IJVhyH5p5Iu6DiAl5MzVmgnzbB7nSarhNueMEcbpTDjLCGaOaZ5cm62A_pPoZTKSCnmcXwIG9M8GuPc6MJkBdMCElJtD9qBoBToHWDL73pBe8R6DNnvRGdn4zemFqaWrf6S0ydhavkgMbVAhkhYC1PLhZFqw8CfrSZoGH_yum0YMeT85jeWzv-tdK5p57GWV4PesZaQ-V8t_ITGwzk0n84bc8ZuJ6bF6wiY_9yi_3R6efU7AAD__yzcjpI), the Associated Press projected yesterday, unseating eight-term Republican Rep. Scott DesJarlais three weeks after Election Day. Broderick, a tech support worker who ran a grassroots campaign without airing any TV ads, led by [fewer than 400 votes out of about 196,000 cast](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSnSAQhZ8GOxxB8GpBkcbuT5vSQVivmyA47F6dvH3GFHmBlN_Mzn7nnB9fy5fHhPn93R_gmLclw00JmKEuhveIxBUD35gz1FDyhvWARXd6kEpJbRcfGC9YjG-iW7WavAkNOPWa7NCZSdlmd-uqtwlUsNZq8FYrvSmjBrPaYVTbaBt0z0OltFWqG_u-7YYQx97aaeon_xo6YTqIyKW2vANDzkAEsKXf5YLahnI0ye3MJ4n-m9Cz0PN93y3jAbRVgLMC0XMm9Pz0E3p-hA-V6wEj9BzhKKF6lhcGLhW9XGuJUDH8kjdmkv-8ci8fAkngWZYPMea3rHBKCoVZRqCfviaPj6apLp43poQ0vITp3ofH9Dcw_-fal9N_AgAA__8ys5aa). DesJarlais [conceded Nov. 16](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkDGu2zAMhk8jbwokWrLjQUMXb-na0VAkOmYjS4HEOujtCxd4ucBbCIL4SP74ft2Wm6dE-fHT7-iY1yXjuyVkxroY3iI1rhT4TTljDSWvVHdcQMEgtZZgFx-YDlyM76K7g568CR06PU52UGbSttvctPZaBRiNiTr4oBDUOAD0EVFfjbUdufOg1mC1Vte-v6ghxGtv7TT1kx8HJYzCSFzqhTdkzBlbQ1zT33JgvYSyd8ltzK8m-h8CZgHzB0qlPMsfPiEB8_lHwKz1Wc4uYvvta_LUZCg5YMQmP7vS8HaOHxVbo5J9kl9CJBcZcS-hepYHBS6VvLzXErFSeAqYu-ri600pURtGYdRj95T-Z-Vvij4c_AsAAP__6d6UcA) after provisional ballots counted in Nashville widened her narrow lead. She's the only Democrat to win a Tennessee U.S. House seat this year, flipping a district President Trump carried by 24 points in 2024.
## Al Gore Buying Hometown Newspaper
Former Vice President Al Gore is [buying the Carthage Courier](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ8GOpC9NiYULq6hy7VXosVsYCVjR2YvVt7-lBT3An830kjfaL4_9-WOHDntv_EkL_JYEtUrkgiVxcqx8SWFg1ROiUrI6cHlpAUUuE7rDoYFg_CLFovt5lfQE9rQktfjNDhlJz20h1cKDViLGldjnAtWO7QIFqZVDQq3lv0HqDUMWqubMb1yYbuZYZgmM-HoVGMVbSy59HKQUEp0XUSP-M4vKn3IZxv9IfK8GvOrgbmBudbav_HI-dM2MH9uNTBjEQ6RvjF2ey7UrX_fnPbuyCdJrqn7j-9AgwOnR90fcsa2-O1ZOUa-3NhYtZ_I8bstPxT38vAvAAD__4sugk8), a 113-year-old newspaper in his Smith County hometown of Carthage that has been family-owned for 50 years. Gore said he wants to preserve the paper as an independent voice for Carthage and Smith County, citing the importance of strong local news. The price of the paper was not mentioned publicly. Before entering politics, [Gore, 78, worked as an Army reporter in Vietnam](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1ugzAUQOGnMVuQ_8GDhyx0SteOlrEv4arGROYK1Lev0lfoeJZvOF-P8IhYsD4_4waeaAkVrqMAEbSgac14UMNEF9YKLe11wbZBkFzamxA3aUJMhCcEHbvsZylc1KkDLwZnLNdOmG71PKlxVtpaKebRCJsHPUCcOdduATtCh_4NCiGNEHxUquc25VEZ45xycbCcaQ4ZaW89rUBQKxwHwFJ-9hNan_atK34leh1M3ZmcmJyg9hd-4wsyxn5vTyandzM53Uv42Bt0zefXhaXgYQem-XOLWP4o-ueH08vfAAAA__9omHFV) and spent five years as a reporter at _The Tennessean_ in Nashville.
## Swift Honors Brenda Lee's Christmas Classic
Taylor Swift [surprised Brenda Lee](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2u2zAQBODTUB0N8UeyVKhIo-6lTSmsyZW1CEU6y7WJd_tAuUK6AQb4MJhfX9sXUKL8_AknLiL7lrHVhCLIm5cjUhWmII1yRg4l78Qnbra3ozZG22GDIPTBzUMXl4c1M_jQ4WLu8zD2fjZDdyyAsM922CdwQzSzMz14HL2fprsLLkwdLRdojB2M6Sfnbv0Y4uSGYZ7dDPexV77HSFL4JgcK5oy1Iu7pu3yQb6GcXVoOkVdV7oeyq7Jra-3W6vm5SmXXy1d2NebKXtlV4DsV1rXRLrq--cVUseoHY46gE6JuJId-JfjzRh0w4YNBKD81l_CbsgYu7xx1OJiqnFC1MKI-KWGVklHZteMlvhqlRHW8K98_T6D0b6z859Ofxf4NAAD__4oglNs) with a Recording Industry Association of America diamond plaque marking 10 million U.S. copies sold of her Christmas classic _Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree._ Lee recorded the song in 1958 at just 13 years old, and it [finally topped the Billboard Hot 100](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL2K4zAYAJ9G7mL0a0eFinDgLlccB1sKRfocf0SWgvRtzL79kn2FLaeZgfm4-mvAjOX-N-zgiFZf4OgZiKB5TVvCTg0jHVgKtFjLim0HL7mcTkKcpPEhEr7A6zAkd5PCBh0HcGK2ZuLaCjNsLsxcpilwHa29rUZrlVRINk4JjLJwHtC9hUJIIwQ_KzXyKaazMsZaZcM8caY5JKTaRtqAoBToHWDNX_UFbYx1H7LbiJ6dqQuTC5MLlPHABz4hYRhruzO5vJnJ5V-NDyxMGjn7S6ufJXnawP_ZGnbaQ_f_G8DQXHoemDP2aWaa3_eA-SdEv7z0cvI7AAD__xD3fRE) in December 2023, 65 years later. It's one of only two Christmas songs to reach diamond status. Lee, 81, lives in the Nashville area and is a member of both the Country Music Hall of Fame and the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame.

## Army Scraps Georgia Firm's Contract
A University of Georgia professor says the U.S. Army [canceled](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhDAQRU9jOiN7jIEtXKSh27Qp0awZs5YMRvZoyd4-IsoN0n_9p_e-7vMdY4r7-okbOV7DvNNZEzFTmbFs7-oLHtXnnQt6PuiosfIMCnqptQQ7o-f4ornDZnFGLaS7sSGnh5vtlVU9NE-HQY8LEGoFZAgGY7Qf6eY9Gj9A1zfRXYdag9VaK3trlXp4HcbBKNOp3gbRKVoi59Lyk1bKZY0Y0ju_qLQ-b01yT-ajCvMhYBIwnefZhvxtkRPujNdGwHSpCZguLZkPrjLmE-UjYWWJgalIj7unK4f8g8gQy1blQpia4pbjjCnF2g-iU-uGMf3S-Z_hXg5-AgAA__8jTIT0) his company's contract to neutralize unstable explosives in Iowa, opting for a controlled detonation Wednesday instead. **Good Morning!** On this day in 1963, President John F. Kennedy was [_buried at Arlington National Cemetery_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0D-uozAQgPHTmM4ID38cCopt6N62W6IhHsMkjh0N80C5_Wr3Cu8Cnz79_nwtX8iJ8_YbXzTpGZdM15FIlWRRwZOSfB_7ShvnQ0iFUCMu0MBgnbPQL3hXPmnpsApTxI5wrGhyfuyHpnf9rdonbHykMDRt66HDHv3NDaMffd-t9ziM94qnfz3noHfOQTvUHpFi40JLwQPcRtM1FFiL1LrTybJxZozpU06S-l5eVZp21fdh2l8GZgPzdV31Iz4Tr4LyqYtsBuZEKNnAjGv5VvuITwPzIz4tZ7vzoUU-BuZcTnqtJBbAunFobSDU3ZZodSf7Fjo4UNZKpvC-OCU-Bm-6Znshp_8r-kPFc4K_AQAA___jKoiX), three days after his assassination in Dallas. His widow, Jacqueline, lit the eternal flame that still burns today. We’ve uncorked a fair amount of [_wine-related content_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAURb8GO4wg4FhQbGM3225pnvLUl6BM4Olk_n7j_sJ2t7on5_w8xydQpGP9hh09X8t44LtEZMY8coYLYz7LNuFKR8nIGYEXGHWjnVRKajvCzHThaKAKfgGD0FfoVddb11hlH9Xmu9mpYLB3JjgztbZHROds5-xkpsmYivz9p5S2SinduroDwKVRocXQaf3ohWkwEKdc84YX5ZUOgiV-0oW5ntNeRb8xv4pov4QehB5myIEOiLdMnfIq9HAjhB6UurcRelhi-gQ5p_PgT5HzBoxwyj3lTOX2l1Tk-ZJLyrJARKGHKvvwelOMVFwnTLPuQPGPz_9Md3n9GwAA__-XQYPV) for you today. How long is that turkey actually safe in your fridge? About 48 million Americans get food poisoning every year, and no week fills more refrigerators with risky leftovers than this one. Today, we're breaking down seven kitchen rules from the CDC and USDA that keep Thanksgiving leftovers from sending you to the hospital. Does the sniff test really work? And why does washing your chicken spread germs across the whole kitchen? Check out _The Flyover Podcast_ to hear the one rule that could save your life. So here’s a fun full-circle moment for Thanksgiving week. Today’s sponsor is Montgomery Ward. ## Thanksgiving Travel Rush Begins
More than [_2 million Virginians will travel_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOozAQhp_GdI5sYyAULq6hy7VXogkeYHTGjuxZZ_P2K7LaJ9h6NJ--7_93m29AgeL2Fw50XNc54rMEZMY8c4aKIX-U_Y4bxZKRMwKvMBtleqm1NN0MC1PF2ULj3QoWYWzQ6WHsetXp7trs7m5X1VqvFIy27a_joKyGXi_YtYO3CzbkTp7WptNam7a_DAC4Ku1b9IMx11FYhZ445QvvWClvFAnW8EoV82VJRxPczvwoov0jzCTM9CzI50GY6ewRZgppgSDMdKSMkneI0siDQqAU5Q8xFomfD1wYveQkv_PlmvL74X_ZqFLc5J4CeXjJmCoed8zytG-y84_nCSz9IKzaDqDwduNfzlqd-QoAAP__wOqQAw) at least 50 miles from home for Thanksgiving, according to AAA, part of a projected 81.5 million Americans traveling nationwide. About 1.88 million will drive, and roughly 128,000 will fly. The Virginia forecast is [_down about 1.5%_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O5CAQhU-DM1pQDf4JCDZxNptuaNWYwi4tjUfAYPn2K08fYdOqT0_ve38-lg_kyGn7jS9ytYUl0Vki1Up5qRkbxfxd9k_aOJVMNRPWgAso6KXWEuyCa-VGi8HOu4CGcOrI6WGyvbLajt3unjQZrexoVgXWWKsBjR8nVIPtVwzYsbvztAartYZn_xgQKSjtn-QHgHESRpHneuRH3alx3jgxhngdjfJjPV5ddHutX0U8fwmYBczneT5ObNf9FDBHbpw2GY8Vo4B5PyJ7vIqAuX5T8XjJt6CsO6a_ZXvjb315-8vPzGm7j5zWTFjISwyVcjqOdIMh8PpDCpi77PzXyTFy6Qdh1PZCjj81638u3Bz8CwAA__-iT5Uu) from last year, a dip AAA ties to higher gas prices and airfare. VDOT is suspending many highway work zones and [_lifting most lane closures_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O5CAQBOCnwRkjwPgvILjE2Vx6odU2bbt1GEbQw2jefjW7j7B5qVT1_bsvd6BA8fgLFzqu-xLxVQIyY144Q8WQn-Vc8aBYMnJG4B0Wo0wvtZamW2BjqrhYaLzbwSJMDTo9TF2vOt2NzemsHe3UeoMDmrW1q8Uetn7tVKdateHYkPv0aW06rbVp-9sAgLvSvkU_GDNOwir0xCnf-MRK-aBIsId3qphvW7qa4E7mRxHtH2FmYeZypoweKLw_dz4RYeYTwQeKWISZq08sOclAO8srFZYBIsotpPLMWOSesuQT4v9yUKV4yB8LYeYmO_94UQhU-kFYdVxA4XsE_9KvOvMVAAD___GXiLE) from noon Wednesday through noon Monday. Drivers can check conditions on the free [_511 Virginia app_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkMGqpDAQAL8m3kaSVqNzyGFh8DZ7WZY9Sms62hCNJL0O8_ePeb_wzgVVUP-e0xM58rH-xp2cXGE66FUiiVCeJONFMf8v20wrHyWTZEIJOIEGezPmBt2Ei_BFU4uVdwFbwntFzvT3zurOdEO1OYBhMBpnawJqGEyPFqCdtYewLMHOFbuPzxjojDHQ2LpHpKCNb8j3AMNdtZo8S8q1bHRxXvlgDPGdLsr1kvYquk3kLKr5pWBUMJ4R3_Wa0hrpwxWMRVImBSOeZ1EwehLkWFQzslfNY0l7vVNmz3jUl0-iwG5RNQ86pr9_quz8-eIYudhetXrdkeN3V3647HLwFQAA___iPYFr). Virginia State Police are stepping up patrols through [_Operation C.A.R.E._](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykUD1vpDAQ_TWmM8IDht3CxTV0e-2VaMBjGK0XVvacUf59RKQ0aVM-Pb3Pf4_pgRx5X__ii5yUMO105kgilCZJWCim_3mbaeU9J5JEKAEnaKDXxmiwEy7ChaYOK-8CdoT3ipwZ7rZvrLG3anNhMdguBmxzm5vWGmuJTD-H0IbBe1wqdpefMWCNMdD29YBIoTG-JT8A3O6qa8izHKmWjQqnlXfGED-OQqlejlcV3Sbyzqr9o2BUMJ7nWZ-Jl4tUMF6bFIzfSv0TZ0Eh_T4iL6QxP7VPXChlLYeeSWcMpK8sLRvuz7xy4X1VMFbJ-ffJMXLuB9U16ws5fhWSX35ZHHwGAAD__9KjjRw), which runs Wednesday through Sunday. Pointing to 18 deaths on state roads over the July Fourth holiday alone, troopers urge travelers to buckle up, slow down, and drive sober.
## Virginia Lands $12.6M for Home Visits
Virginia’s Department of Health has been [_awarded $12.6 million_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkbGunTAQRL_GdHtlL2BDQZGG7qVNiRa8vqxk8JVxjPL3EZHyBa8djc7oaH59LV8kUc73Tzp4KjUsJ99X5FI4LyVT5Zh_X_vKbzmvzCUzlUALarRgDGC_0Fak8tJR46dAHdPY8GTc2Fvdm35o9qnzeuPgjQ1Wk9106zY7doPzdtjQrGMj08MzBntjDLb25Yg4aONb9g5xGFWn2UtJ-VV2rpLfcgqF-CdVzq8tHU2c9lI-l2p_KJwVzvd9v0z7qJzpfhoKZ8pFtsgK5ydXOO9MsewK5_9EyLyxVL7AoIVDYpR0wienKp4hZGbY08FQ5ZJyQUlwpMwQ6JAo_CBxNEA8DM57B62lAB2tK4y217BqM7bOodPsmzz5z_0MXNapTr8PkvjPpHzzhDrh3wAAAP__fz6cRg) in federal funding to expand free, voluntary home visits for new and expecting parents in at-risk communities. The grant, from the federal [_Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting program_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OpDAQBOCngcwIGzAQOLiEbC69EPXgxm7JPyPTZzRvf5qTNth486pPpfrz2B9AgZL7DREN13NPeF8BmbHsXKBiKH8v_0RH6SrIBYFP2FWvtJBSqGmHg6niPkJrzQkjwtqikfM66X6S09J6A6tWy4L9aLU8tO2VPvCpJdjnKI9hhZbMx5NSTVJKNehuBsCzl3ZAOyu1rM3YoyXOpWOPlYqjRHCGd65YuiPHNhjP_Lqa4VejtkZt93131fruK9u5XBu1nRApvIXPEUWli5iSa9QWgbEkCILSCYkFJCsQSniLw1OwPmf7vSNeJbsCUUTCw3_kthj7uikEuvTcjL2LQOH_NP7hq9WofwEAAP__fMORIg), pairs families with nurses, social workers, and parent educators. Visits cover parenting education, developmental screenings for young children, and referrals to local support services. The money is [_expected to extend services_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL_unDAQhJ_GdEbYHHAULtLQ_dKmRAte45X8B9kbn-7to4tSJHXa0cyn0ffja_8CCpSu7xDRcHN7wlcNyIxl5wINQ_lZ_YEXpVqQCwI72PWgZ6mU1NMOJ1PD_QGdNQ4eCGuHRi3rNA-Tmp6dN5OdDsB5hXEeDrcou4Id4RyeoKxyOHZkPjyl9KSU0uPcLwDoBmVHtIvWz1U8BrTEufTssVG5KBG48M4NS3_m2AXjme8qxm9Cb0Jv8fRH70uF_spN6O0u-SoQq6R4w8l_JUJvPkeUjSoxpeszBsaSIEhKDhJLhBLe8vQUrM_Zyn_6MhKevsk_PKE399azhBcUW7ti7P2iEKjOi3gMVwQKvw_zf7puRv8KAAD__8l6mWs) to more than 1,700 families, up from nearly 1,400 during the previous grant year. Virginia runs the program through a [_public-private partnership_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DtuhDAQANDTQLeIGQNeChdpttu0Ka1ZPIaRzEdmYrS3j5Ir5AKveF9P_yRJss2ftLLTEv3G15lYlbPXTIVT_j6XF8-ynZk1M2kkjy0ON4Ab9p4mlcK-ozq4SB3TWLMDO_ZD20N_rxc3hNBZ87JoDAwjmT5AxC4Y04IJ9Iq1uF8PAHsAQDM0lohjC8FwsIj3sepaDqJ7bnThInmWTSim9144N9O-1sktqsdZmY8KHxU-rutqmHJ6y3rQpIWaPc8VPlbhaSl1duG4JCU5B1t17bySpD9H_1lQHP4EAAD__74Pce0) with Early Impact Virginia. Home visiting is voluntary and offered at no cost to families.
## 1,145 Acres Protected along the Pamunkey
A conservation group has [_permanently protected 1,145 acres_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OwyAQRk-DOyLA_wXFNu6y7ZbWBMY2EgZrmDjK7VdeKSfYboqn90bfz32-Q4ghrd-wo-VzmRO-SkRmpJkJToz0LNsD15AKIRMCLzAbZTqptTTtDI7DiXMDlbcLNAhjhVb3Y9upVrdDtVnwLT76h_IwNBoVoBvQY-3V0A5NXY9VsJdPa9NqrU3d3XoAXJT2NfremGEUjUIfONONNzwDrSEFWOI7n0g3l_cq2o35KKL-EmYSZvowO5J70vtihJmuijCT1tfdCDNFSF66nArSCRxykivl5yEPpB0SJo5veVBmdFzkFZNaKSXBERaZF7mFwpmCk5-eXID2yyrMVJH1xyvEGErXi0atO4T49y3_c-jTmt8AAAD__0avlfI) of Retreat Farm, a working farm on the Pamunkey River that has stayed in the same family since the 1700s. The [_Capital Region Land Conservancy_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkb2upjoMRZ8GOqPE_HykoLgN3bntlMgEByKFBCU-oPP2I0aaJ5jOhbX2Xtq_vpYv8sHH_X86eZLbLZGfEliE8yKZbg75uxwr7z6WzJKZxNGCCgfQGrBfyIq_eemo3iZHHZOpedIf0w-q1_1YHxOiM51iZVvdDtvIbmVcDRrHrse2G2s_vTytsddaYzs0HyJ2Sm8tbx_E0VSd4s1Lyo0cfPu8--jJhZ90c25sOuswHSJXqdr_KpwrnJ_naexatHlt3o8K5_escC5CwhXOgeIGNsXC-SbxKcKe0_cFF-eTIkcJP3DlJGylwBsEGpRSQDZzgeTg8EVS9hb-FgJH-XyxFc6UxdvAi9Gr7YatBeoVQr-2BGbgETZF3TqSaZVVzSFnqPO0XY8PwZfhU3VqP8mHP27yj7PcE_4OAAD___pXpGY) announced the easement Monday, calling it the largest in its history. The deal was made possible in part through the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Natural Resources Conservation Service. Located along the Hanover–New Kent county line, Retreat Farm has been farmed for more than 375 years and still grows crops on 452 acres. The easement blocks future development while allowing farming to continue. The family has owned it since the 1700s; the Blackwells sold it in 1772 to [_Carter Braxton_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L9ugzAQgPGngS3I_8Bh8NAlW7p2RAec4SRjR-cLad--Sl-h-6ff8H3dpztQorx9woFBzjhlfNWEIsiTMJyY-Fn3GTfKlVEYQSJMRpnhovXF9BMsQidODto1RHAIY4tB-7EfVK_7a7sHiA6jj6PzRtlhNt6itf3irAU1D-7aUnh7Wptea23s0HkAjEqvFldvzHVsnMKVpHAnO57EG2WCmH7Kidwt5WhT2EUetbEfjbk15raUXIXkKVTyglmQu8JbY26Vtoxc3wmwIF9mhm8pueWwPl6UEtXBN05tB1D6o-WfV85gfgMAAP__qk95RA), a signer of the Declaration of Independence.
| Flying together with our sponsor [](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2K6zAQRp9G7hI0o7-4UHEhpMtttzQTa2QLFCdIsw779kvyCtt-fJwD5-s6XanUsi3_6c5R9jxt_OqVRbhN0mjn2r77euOlbL2xNCbJNKFGfwA4oJtolrLzZGlIMZNlGgeOEEbntQN3GtaYQ6ZkZtY3jdq7WwBiZ-cxWXIQnB9KfPMA0AEAGn8MRJw1JMMpIJ5GZTWnIo92lJX30payFcr157FzO86P-1DjKvLsyvxTeFF4afyilmaulT6H92oupMwZbNAK_azMGdGPTqHvoMy5CwkPLabnq9Raug_K6uVOpX4E8sc2e8TfAAAA__-ep3aq) **Remember the Montgomery Ward Christmas Wish List?**

## Counted Ballots Flip House Seat
Jonathan Bradner, D, [unseated Rep. Cindy Abrams](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFyhCAQxvGn0Q4HELizoEhjd2lTOissJzMoDuxp8vYZr8gL5AV2f9__6zE9IKa4PT9hRUt5CdOGZ01IhGWaIaVMLr82qiHFvSJQhUR1klwaJgSTegJH8cBJQeutwl6EoUUrboM2XCuu28VKjnpw2il_753XdwTQsjcwKxf0zYg22uueEFILIYzqOy703Rs1G8dFCObWKI4-Ui4dLZiXmEP6yQeWzuW1TXYh2mvTfzRybOR4nmd3Ht-vLpdnI8c9p0jR1UaOf2rVyHEu4DcszGO4ZjGYC6yVhVzY9YFVAkK25FdF5mOlEh0xObArQlus38-YUqxv3HOFmN4Y-m_Ew8rfAAAA__8S44fQ), R, Harrison, after the Hamilton County Board of Elections reversed course Tuesday and counted about 740 disputed provisional ballots. Abrams had led by 19 votes, within automatic recount range. With the ballots added, Bradner won by enough to avoid a recount, and the board certified the results. The ballots came from voters who moved to Hamilton County from elsewhere in Ohio without updating their registrations, then voted at their new polling places. ## Army to Detonate Iowa Explosives Today
The Army is set to detonate nearly five tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown [at 9 a.m. CT today](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL_GdCDWGHMuXKShu7Qpkc9ejs0Z-wIrrMvXR6TJB6QbaaQ3mvdxna6OIqX7u1vR8pynhGWPyIzbRLm4gJyTY8qJF5ce-50OSpNspa4BatlPzjMdOEEV7IwosavQwmB63erOmGqxiPo2ez8rFbTxYIzEoNub6S9tbwZ1q8ieOADZA3QdDA2YNpih8w4uyijTCdViIM5b85kp8YJzfOUDt8bntYp2YX7uonsTchRyLKU0j_Llz1LI8UQLOQKcWQk5Mq1Y78h1wZBwD-5VR3Shdt8UsP67K-RYbTY8C8VIux6Eau-ro_g7yv9TdVj5EwAA__80MHyQ). Residents within five miles southwest of the plant may be evacuated, and those up to 20 miles out are told to stay inside with windows closed. A federal appeals court on Monday [cleared the blast](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZCC6bcw4cHAJ2Vx6ITJ2e_CdsUfQB9q_X7HJfsBmJZX0Sq_-POenSzmV12-3keVY50LXkYmZ9jnVywXiWhynWnh15d_xSmcqM_aoW4AWh9l5TifN0AQbiZBkQxZGM-heS2Oa1dIjRj0qbaIKAbAfgvFRRlyQBjA6NMneOAAcAKSEsQPTBzNK7-ChjDJSqJ5C4rp3f2sqvFLMH_WkvfN1a7Jdmd-HkL8ETgKn67o6XxZ_lwKnGy1wArizEjjdUu23VbvUbWl9_b9z26285Wa34X2lnNOhR6H61-ZS_lrin_1zWvwMAAD__92heKE), rejecting environmental groups' bid to block the emergency EPA permit. The Army says the 68 barrels, stored for more than 20 years, are [too unstable to move](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHunDAMxp8mbDnFDhAyZOiS7d-1I8oRc6QN5ER8IN6-oqrUB-hmWdbP3-_78TV-hZTT9voeVnI8l3Gjs2Zipn1M5QyRuGyBU9l4Cduv-kpH2kZU2EsAid0YJk4HjdBENxMh6YYcGNv1qtfWNoujMCswth2Gp9LP2ZhBP_sZO6UNtEOvmuRuHAB2AFqDeYBV0Ro9BRha21otWkUxcdkfP0vaeKE5X-Wg_TGVtcluYX5Xob8J9AL9eZ6PTw1cYrjuA4G-ctkvgf5WE-hvLYH-firQA9yz_ruXmUKU_6Tl5x0Dk5zKZ2eZ08xVVg6XDPt6Iy1arQ30ShmBvtldfJ8p51R7I1r1WkPKf1Ly_3V7OPwdAAD__wLqiy4) and more likely to explode on their own as temperatures fall. President Trump had ordered the Army to [hold off](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE8DGchugz0OHGxCNptuiLymGXrX2CPTg8Xtv_hX-EmppJKqVO_Pc356ipRev_2Ojtc8J6xHRGYsM-XqF-ScPFNOvPn0_3jRSWkGAbqTsoNx9oHpxFm2i1sRAVWLTho7aqGVte3mjFWg9GAXMej1EfRfra0eR2lWHRYwpiV310kJo5RKSdNLKxZrVPDyMdjBqmYQuBDn0v_LlHjDNV75xNKHvLfRbczvo1G_GpgamGqt_eW3nO-0gen-08D0ucUXphDxtiF_Cnchoi9HV_3VfY7Ol_3qhBhAGgVjv_Ee2-KWd6UY6dCmGcRr9xS_d_lntE4HXwEAAP__NMB9XQ) until the court ruled and said Democrat Gov.-elect Rob Sand should also agree. Sand said the call belongs to the administration.
## Storm Threatens Travel, Macy's Balloons
A nor'easter that forecasters fear could strengthen into a "[bomb cyclone](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZB7htoFx4OASsrn0QuTBDfSdsUd2C8Tfn9ho881KKump6v15TS9PkdL62-_oeMlTwrNGZMYyUT59QM7JM-XEm0__6koHpQla6KVSErrJz0wHTqoJbkEE1A06Ndiub3ttbbO5oO1sjFFghhBseJvhbZ9g1HO2BvoOG3I3TinolNJaDQ9l22AHPXv1NNZYLUyLgTiXx99MiTdc4pUPLI857010G_OnCv1LwChgTNcnV74rAeMNFjAqdWcjYIy0YOUrooDx26FVcvEHRnmi5w2LPCkxFlk5l71Kn4IMGP1V5ZILzr6ygLEpLnxOipFqPwjTrrun-LWJf2bycPA_AAD__7j4iDc)," a storm that intensifies rapidly as its pressure plunges, will hit Florida and the Carolinas today before slamming the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast on Thanksgiving Day, as 81.5 million Americans travel for the holiday. The giant balloons at the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, which marks its 100th anniversary with 100 inflatables, [cannot fly](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uxCAQhJ8Gd5xY8B8FRaTI3aWJopTWnsH2JhhOQGz57aO7Kn3q0Yzm-z6v4xXJU1jecHOmzHEM7sjeleLSSPFA60oMWCiGsmL4zgvtFEYpZMsBuGxGnArtboTKmtk56VTlDHS6aUWrtK5WA10_i6ax3a1TGoXtlXQaa9AzzFbWU0XmMQcgGwCloLuAFlZ3akLoa11rxWrhLJWYLl-RQlnd7M-4u3SZ4lZ5s5Zyz0y9MDkwOeBteiA8MiaHj3cmh1xSDAs_KNjMlxR_guUbTmfmf5gWbvHkd0xoHb-h9zGG_CzHdDI1kGXqFVRfgwTRVsnY-0HeU247VotlQ_LPP-V_FncjfwMAAP__hgmG6w) if sustained winds top 23 mph or gusts exceed 34 mph. The NYPD makes the final call. Forecasters expect [flight delays](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD3PnDAQhH8NdIv8wce5cJGG7k2bEq1gDX5jbGTvYd2_jy7XpE87M5rRM7--li_0wcf9J55k2aUlUi2BmCkvPlXciFNE9inygfF32f3t46KEGkFKUMOCK_ubFtlu1hEp0i1ZOZlhFKM2pj2sfBhH0vSTc0pQP-jBTWIgacaxNwZ16-27Tko1SKm1nDppxGYmvaJ89KY3uukFbZ5T7r6Tj3yQC690U-7WdLbBHsxXafSPRs2NmmutHa7rsxLy8ck0aqb4tj4SuJRpxcKlUfOJ3ynDP2w7FE75BE5QIuYAnPGmAFjgSpWyewaoPm4FDsL7BRl9hFKJLiAsTDnCSpEzBni-B6QZ1SAebbbbVX0IvoxT04v9RB_-AvD_3X5b9ScAAP__J22aeQ) to spread from Orlando and Miami today to Washington, Philadelphia, New York, Boston, Detroit, and Chicago on Thursday, with cancellations likely peaking on Thanksgiving. [Wind gusts over 50 mph](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAMhp8GuqA4QDIpUlwz3Vx7JfIQA7kNySixQPP2K3ab7bez_FnW__3_HtMDQwxp_Ys7OV7ylOiskZipTCGf6IlzQg458Ybpo67hCGlSUmkBINQ44czhoAla7xYiRX1LDowdtdS9te3m7KDs-NTqBlKRHsdRLmTIw82A9jjYNrjrHYAaAfoeTAdWemv6GeE22MH2zSDJB86l-59D4o2W-M4HlW7OexvdxvyqTf-nUfdG3c_z7NJzvjQufm0IeaPSqHvlXPZ6DXRQIfFDaRXfUPBWCJmS2EOMIacquOBBkUoVO87vKl5Y0JMoc0INIA20xfnXeZ1XbZpBrjuG-BWOf1fp4dRnAAAA__9Jk43E) are forecast across the Northeast, with downed trees and power outages expected, and major coastal flooding is likely along the Atlantic. The balloons have been fully grounded only once, in 1971.
## Map: Favorite Thanksgiving Pies by State
Cream pies, a catch-all that covers everything from banana to Indiana's sugar cream, are the most distinctly popular variety in nine states, more than any other kind, according to a new map of [Thanksgiving pie orders by state](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQBb_GdCCvDQYXLtLQXdqUyIcX2MRnI7wB3d9Hlyp9-qc3mvm4TTdPkdL67h_oeMlTwqtEZMZjonz5gJyTZ8qJN5--ykonpUlJZWqAWnWTn5lOnKAKbkFUqCt00NvOSKOtrTYnjemUAVBohzAM8m7k3Yal7-Rg-tnqitzrDkB1AFpD34CVwfZ69jC0trVatBIDcT6az0yJN1ziM594NHN-VNFtzHsR-k2oUajxuq7mpPLt4-x3Yh-p8Gso1PjHYK13wlLfn3VhzyjUWB0u7BfFSMX0opXrw1P8JfD_upxO_QQAAP__vWd31w) released over the weekend. The rankings come from [grocery orders](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OozAURp8GOiP8A8SFi23osu2W6Ma-wN0YG9lXRHn7UaaafvpPn845_-7LHShS2v7CgY7XvCR81YjMWBbKLwjIOQFTTrxDetaNLkqL6tUopBRqWMAzXbjINrgVUaFu0cnJDmM_amvb3Sk0aG8GVt8j-F7i9FDjDYxXEPQQ1pbc505KNUiptZw6aftgJ-1B3ow1Vjemx0CcS_c_U-Id1_jOF5bO56ONbmc-a6P_NGpu1OzzcUJ6d5Qqg4fCn1Wj5gAMggumUBs1I9S3gCpOQgEi5vwUwOKH4lbFkSuLB8Z8YRABa8XCbXHhfFGMVMepMf12AMVvDv5dvcuprwAAAP__SumHfA) placed during Thanksgiving week in 2024, and they measure which pies a state buys at unusually high rates, not which pies sell the most. Apple pie, second nationally, tops no state at all. French silk, a chocolate pie under whipped cream, is the standout in seven states clustered in the Midwest, including Illinois, Iowa, and Nebraska. Sweet potato and pecan split the South, and pumpkin wins out West. The Thanksgiving pie rush is in full swing. Orders for pumpkin, pecan, and sweet potato climb through late November, and the day before Thanksgiving is the biggest pie-buying day of the year. ## Chlorine Detected Outside Deer Park Plant
Harris County Pollution Control [detected minor traces of chlorine](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSpCAURb8GMyzeAxQCgk3MZtMNLYTnyAxKF9Jt9379Vu8vTHyrbp1z_nzMHz7ldHz-9ju59lzLfNB1ZmqN6vxFtb6-ykFnLIdvdEqxb-dayowCBw7AUc8-tPSgGbroFhEtdORgtHoQRoDuNocqDMqrIM0SwUQpgkC7glJG06ht6JJ7vwGgBhQCsDejVoNdrTc6yjhYpgTF1Ert20aNnv5c86s8qPah7F12W2u3k8lfDCeG03Vd_fdW7u-R4eRrSyETw-ktxnDKJfjMcIpEld98_eb5vtT0t2QeNtpT8JmnI6RIR-MllspwQqO51dKDMYaPBgxXOAD3XlpOSGGNEsYFVVddvF0p53QOI1Pic_cp_6dsP4z7cPgvAAD__yvTi1I) outside the fence line of Lubrizol's Deer Park plant Tuesday morning, but city officials said the levels were safe and posed no threat to the surrounding community. The leak began just after 10 a.m., and Lubrizol hasn't said what caused it or whether anyone was hurt. Pemex's nearby Deer Park refinery briefly [issued a shelter-in-place alert](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGS4yAQRL8GZbhgJLAVKLiEbC-9UIVhtGIXMS4YW9Z9_ZXuFzbroKtfd__5mD98yql8_vYbTvxeaC64t4zMWOcvrPX4ooItUvGMrVfb2haiGRRYqbUEM_vA6YWz7uJ0V3HUHU76Ohqrbkqbbp0iaHtFMwzY936JN4N3fdcWgzVgRrBdms40rcFoUErD5XY1gx2X0d9M7KMdxaAwJqZ64RUZ374t-aAX1kugrcvTyvxoov8lwAlw-75fQk7hG1Z6NqZyugS4c5cAlyn4LMCdTAFO61MPAlxErPLh67fcqJy0JgvuMpWQIhaWnmV-3mv6S1k-si8smz-aLCR5rehZMslA2_YsiQ8BrqtTfOwp59TsVQzqc_Mp_2_MPzz6NcG_AAAA__9NbJM6) for its own site, lifting it six minutes later. Austin's CrowdStrike Buying Zscaler for $44B Austin-based CrowdStrike, the cybersecurity company at the center of the largest global IT outage ever in 2024, is buying California cloud security firm Zscaler in an all-stock . It's CrowdStrike's , pairing its device protection with Zscaler's network security. CEO George Kurtz called it a "winning combination," but CrowdStrike shares fell about 9% on Monday amid concerns that issuing new stock would shrink current investors' stakes. Zscaler's founder, Jay Chaudhry, will continue to run the company and join CrowdStrike's board. CrowdStrike expects within 18 to 24 months of closing and about $1 billion a year in added sales within 30 months. The deal also expands the Austin company's overseas footprint, uniting in Israel and technology from nine Israeli startups the two companies have bought in recent years. Both companies will operate independently until the deal closes in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028. For Black Friday, take with code through November 29. | ➤ Statewide: Republican U.S. Sen. John Cornyn and U.S. Rep. Michael McCaul, R-Austin, questioned Nvidia's rehiring of CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned Nov. 12 amid reports of an affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. The Trump administration told Nvidia's board he's not a security risk. () ➤ Statewide: Democrats won an 8-7 State Board of Education majority after Republican Audrey Young conceded her District 8 seat Nov. 21. Republicans held 11 of 15 seats before the election. Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa plans to replace Education Commissioner Mike Morath. () ➤ El Paso: The FBI plans to downgrade El Paso's field office, one of two on the southern border, and move leadership to Albuquerque, said U.S. Rep. Veronica Escobar, D-El Paso. She asked Director Kash Patel to reverse it. The FBI hasn't commented. () ➤ Statewide: Texas Cyber Command signed up 63 private companies to help guard water and wastewater utilities from hackers for free. Muleshoe, whose water tank overflowed after Russia-linked hackers broke into its controls in 2024, may use the program. () ➤ Dallas: Federal prosecutors charged three men, including two Georgia prison inmates on contraband phones, in a $1 million jury duty scam. Callers threatened arrest and demanded Bitcoin ATM deposits from victims, including Dallas, Fort Worth, Keller, and Greenville residents. () ➤ San Antonio: The San Antonio Food Bank is serving about 30,000 more people this Thanksgiving, a 17% jump. CEO Eric Cooper cited federal funding cuts and SNAP restrictions. **The Book and the Bet**
John Gray's 'Men Are from Mars, Women Are from Venus' (1992) has sold more than fifteen million copies on a single claim: men and women are motivated by different emotional currencies. Men, Gray says, seek trust, acceptance, appreciation, admiration, approval, and encouragement -- status, competence, the satisfaction of fixing things alone in the cave. Women seek caring, understanding, respect, devotion, validation, and reassurance -- connection, being heard, the point-scoring of relationship. His men retreat and act; his women talk and relate.
Academics have never been kind to the book. The linguist Deborah Cameron ('The Myth of Mars and Venus') and the psychologist Janet Hyde (whose "gender similarities" research found men and women alike on most psychological traits) treat Gray as _pop astrology_ : unfalsifiable, endlessly anecdotes, useless for predicting any actual person. And they are right -- about individuals. No wife votes as Gray would predict; no husband does either.
But Gray's claim is, at bottom, a prediction about _aggregate priorities_. And there is exactly one institution in American life that measures aggregate priorities with precision, every four years, in booth after booth across fifty states. If Gray is right about anything, it should show up there.

### How America's Gender Gap Flipped -- and What 2026's Muslim Vote Shows

**The Book and the Bet**
John Gray's 'Men Are from Mars, Women Are from Venus' (1992) has sold more than fifteen million copies on a single claim: men and women are motivated by different emotional currencies. Men, Gray says, seek trust, acceptance, appreciation, admiration, approval, and encouragement -- status, competence, the satisfaction of fixing things alone in the cave. Women seek caring, understanding, respect, devotion, validation, and reassurance -- connection, being heard, the point-scoring of relationship. His men retreat and act; his women talk and relate.
Academics have never been kind to the book. The linguist Deborah Cameron ('The Myth of Mars and Venus') and the psychologist Janet Hyde (whose "gender similarities" research found men and women alike on most psychological traits) treat Gray as _pop astrology_ : unfalsifiable, endlessly anecdotes, useless for predicting any actual person. And they are right -- about individuals. No wife votes as Gray would predict; no husband does either.
But Gray's claim is, at bottom, a prediction about _aggregate priorities_. And there is exactly one institution in American life that measures aggregate priorities with precision, every four years, in booth after booth across fifty states. If Gray is right about anything, it should show up there.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5e63e0bd-edf4-4df6-8d7b-f850ac0bb800?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In 2024, it showed up like never before.
**Two Electorates**
In the Edison exit poll reported by Rutgers' Center for American Women and Politics and the Roper Center, women split for Kamala Harris 53-45 while men split for Donald Trump 55-43\. A ten-point gender gap -- with the majority of each sex standing on opposite sides of the same election.
Pew Research Center's validated-voter analysis puts the split even sharper: men backed Trump 55 percent (a twelve-point margin), women backed Harris by seven. And among the youngest voters, the poles fully separated. Tufts' CIRCLE tabulation of the 18-29 exit poll found young women going Harris 58-40 while young men went Trump 56-42 -- a gap of roughly thirty points between two people standing in the same voting line, products of the same schools, the same economy, the same culture.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e120e2f4-9ba9-4760-be9c-c311eb5012ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Unmarried women and married men form the outermost blocs of the entire electorate. On abortion, guns, health care, immigration, and the meaning of strength, the two sexes in 2024 were not disagreeing within a shared frame. They were voting from two different frames -- Gray's two planets, rendered in electoral cartography.
**The Flip Nobody Remembers**
Here is what most commentary misses: this polarity is historically upside-down.
For most of the twentieth century, women who voted were _more_ conservative than men -- what political scientists call the "traditional gender gap," driven by religiosity and traditionalism. In 1948, women leaned Republican. As late as 1976, the sexes voted nearly identically. The modern gap did not exist.
Then, across the 1960s and 1970s, three forces collided: second-wave feminism, women's rising education and wage work, and a party realignment on gender itself. The Equal Rights Amendment passed Congress in 1972. Roe v. Wade was decided in 1973. By 1980 the Democratic platform was pro-ERA and pro-choice while Ronald Reagan's GOP was anti-ERA and anti-abortion. That election produced the first modern gender gap -- men went for Reagan by double digits; women did not -- and in every single election since, women have voted more Democratic than men, by ten to thirteen points in _every_ cycle since 2016.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ea25fc21-0c8f-4b70-96e2-a1b463af1464?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The critical fact for understanding what changed is _how_ American women diverged when Roe and the ERA were the live issues. They diverged _against male-led institutions_. The machinery of the era was women claiming autonomous ballots: NOW and Bella Abzug's generation of congresswomen mobilizing one direction, Phyllis Schlafly's STOP-ERA pulling religious conservative women the other. Either way, the old norm of the "family vote" -- the husband's ballot as the household's proxy -- stayed dead. Surveys of married couples from the 1970s onward show wives simply not following husbands. American women's votes moved away from their men, their pastors, and their party machines, precisely because gender-rights questions made the ballot a matter of individual conscience.
The gender gap, in other words, was never a demographic accident. It was the electoral shadow of women's independence.
**Dearborn, Hamtramck, Minneapolis, Columbus**
Which brings us to 2024's most under examined story: how Muslim American communities in the Midwest voted, and how they were mobilized.
**Michigan.** Dearborn -- the capital of Arab America -- flipped, going Trump 42 percent, Harris 36, Jill Stein 18, according to the New York Times. Hamtramck, the only Muslim-run city in America, went hard for Trump. Its mayor, Amer Ghalib, became the first Muslim or Arab-American official to endorse Trump, and was later named a White House adviser on Arab-American affairs. The "Abandon Harris" campaign delivered its message from the Friday-prayer pulpit at the American Muslim Center in Dearborn, while the advocacy group Emgage campaigned for Harris -- an intra-community fight playing out in religious space. Nationally, CAIR's exit poll of 1,575 verified Muslim voters found Stein 53 percent, Trump 21, Harris 20: a seismic break from a half-century of Democratic alignment, driven overwhelmingly by Gaza.
**Minnesota.** The Somali community of Minneapolis -- the heart of Ilhan Omar's district -- was heavily mobilized through mosque and community networks, torn between Harris, Trump, and third parties, as the Sahan Journal documented. The community's new salience produced a train of viral controversies: a state election official's Somali-language TV message that ignited an integrity row; conservative influencers staging niqab-clad "voter fraud" stunts at polling places that ended with a criminal probe -- of the influencers, not the voters. The Washington Post fact-checked the "widespread illegal Somali voting" allegations as false, or at least unproven.
**Ohio.** Columbus holds one of the country's largest Somali communities. Viral clips alleging translators or elders steering voters circulated in 2024 and after, but no mainstream reporting substantiated systematic directed balloting there.
Running underneath all of it was a repeated claim on social media: that imams told men their wives' votes would follow theirs, that husbands carried the household ballot, that these communities voted as blocs under male instruction. The documented reality is more interesting than the rumor -- and in one structural sense, the rumor's critics and its believers can both claim a piece of it.
**The Structure Was Mars. The Votes Weren 't.**
What is true: in Dearborn, Hamtramck, Minneapolis, and Columbus, votes were organized through male-led institutions -- imams, male mayors, mosque networks, male-led campaigns like Abandon Harris. Bloc endorsement, pulpit mobilization, community discipline. That is a genuinely different mobilization structure from 1972-1982 America, when women's votes were organized _outside_ male clerical authority and broke from male voters. Anyone who wants to see a contrast with the Roe and ERA era has a real one to point at: single-issue communal politics brokered through the mosque as political machine, versus the autonomous women's politics American women built for themselves after they won the vote.
What is not true -- or at least not supported by the best data we have -- is the strong version: that the women voted as the men asked. ISPU's American Muslim Poll 2025, the most careful post-election look at the community, found that 42 percent of Muslim men voted for Trump, against just 17 percent of Muslim women. That is a twenty-five-point gender gap _inside_ the community -- two and a half times the national gender gap. Muslim women did not follow the men into Trump. They split from them even harder than American women split from American men, and stayed overwhelmingly anti-Trump while the men surged. The community's internal divisions ran along lines -- race, class, generation -- that had nothing to do with male direction: nearly half of white Muslims voted Trump; Black Muslims stayed heavily Democratic.
Two years later, with governor's mansions and statehouses at stake instead of the presidency, the National Exit Poll put Muslim voters at 87 percent Democratic, and CAIR's exit survey found the community had "overwhelmingly backed Democrats" -- men and women alike, converging on the same slates: Jocelyn Benson for governor and Abdul El-Sayed for Senate in Michigan, where El-Sayed carried Dearborn by sixty-five points on the highest turnout in the city's recorded history, and a record bench of Muslim women down the ballot -- Ilhan Omar re-elected by widening margins, Zaynab Mohamed in Minnesota, Munira Abdullahi in Ohio. The 2024 gulf between Muslim men and Muslim women shrank to something pollsters could no longer cleanly measure. Whether one reads that as women voting in line with their community's men, or as men streaming back to the column the women had never left -- the likelier reading, since women were already more than eight in ten anti-Trump in 2024 -- the Mars-and-Venus fact is the same: inside this community, the gender gap existed only for as long as Trump's own name was on the ballot. Take him off, and the two planets were suddenly standing in the same polling booth, marking the same ovals.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/395196ce-1393-4e15-b5a1-0b30c42bd6de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So the 2024 Midwest story is not "men told women how to vote." It is: men moved drastically on a foreign-policy issue through institutions men lead, and women -- starting from the same pews -- refused to move nearly as far.
**The Point, Stated Plainly**
1\. Gray's thesis got its best-ever empirical support in 2024. Men and women voted at opposite poles nationally -- ten points apart, majorities on opposite sides -- and roughly thirty points apart among the young. That is a complete inversion of the pre-1960s pattern, when women were the _more_ conservative bloc and the sexes voted alike.
2\. The inversion was manufactured by the Roe and ERA realignment, and its engine was women's independence from male-led institutions. Every gender gap since 1980 is the residue of that independence.
3\. The Muslim-community vote in Michigan, Minnesota, and Ohio is the mirror image in structure: ballots brokered through male-led religious and municipal institutions around a single issue. Yet even there, the women broke from the men -- by twenty-five points. Gray's Venus survives even where the mobilization structure looks like Mars.
Gray's book is not social science, and a gap is an average that no individual voter owes anyone. And the viral claims of directed voting were mostly unverified or outright fabricated stunts; the documented story is communal bloc politics plus an enormous intra-community gender split -- not proof that Muslim women voted on their husbands' instructions.
The deeper irony is worth closing on. The Roe and ERA era taught America that women's votes diverge from men's when women claim their own ballots. 2024 suggests the divergence is now permanent -- ten points nationally, thirty among the young, twenty-five inside a community where no one predicted it. Mars and Venus are not communicating better. They are voting further apart than at any time since women first entered the electorate -- and the one place where men's votes and women's votes most nearly converged last November was the place where men's institutions did the most organizing.
**Sources** : Edison Research exit polls via Rutgers CAWP and the Roper Center; Pew Research Center validated-voter study (2025); Tufts CIRCLE youth exit-poll analysis; New York Times (Dearborn results); BBC News (Abandon Harris, Dearborn); Al Jazeera (Amer Ghalib endorsement); CAIR 2024 national exit poll; ISPU American Muslim Poll 2025; Sahan Journal (Minnesota Muslims); Washington Post fact-check on Somali voting allegations.

A ten-point gender gap -- with the majority of each sex standing on opposite sides of the same election. Pew Research Center's validated-voter analysis puts the split even sharper: men backed Trump 55 percent (a twelve-point margin), women backed Harris by seven. And among the youngest voters, the poles fully separated. Tufts' CIRCLE tabulation of the 18-29 exit poll found young women going Harris 58-40 while young men went Trump 56-42 -- a gap of roughly thirty points between two people standing in the same voting line, products of the same schools, the same economy, the same culture. | | ---|---|--- Unmarried women and married men form the outermost blocs of the entire electorate. On abortion, guns, health care, immigration, and the meaning of strength, the two sexes in 2024 were not disagreeing within a shared frame. They were voting from two different frames -- Gray's two planets, rendered in electoral cartography. The Flip Nobody Remembers Here is what most commentary misses: this polarity is historically upside-down. For most of the twentieth century, women who voted were more conservative than men -- what political scientists call the "traditional gender gap," driven by religiosity and traditionalism. In 1948, women leaned Republican. As late as 1976, the sexes voted nearly identically. The modern gap did not exist. Then, across the 1960s and 1970s, three forces collided: second-wave feminism, women's rising education and wage work, and a party realignment on gender itself. The Equal Rights Amendment passed Congress in 1972. Roe v. Wade was decided in 1973. By 1980 the Democratic platform was pro-ERA and pro-choice while Ronald Reagan's GOP was anti-ERA and anti-abortion. That election produced the first modern gender gap -- men went for Reagan by double digits; women did not -- and in every single election since, women have voted more Democratic than men, by ten to thirteen points in every cycle since 2016. | | ---|---|--- The critical fact for understanding what changed is how American women diverged when Roe and the ERA were the live issues. They diverged against male-led institutions. The machinery of the era was women claiming autonomous ballots: NOW and Bella Abzug's generation of congresswomen mobilizing one direction, Phyllis Schlafly's STOP-ERA pulling religious conservative women the other. Either way, the old norm of the "family vote" -- the husband's ballot as the household's proxy -- stayed dead. Surveys of married couples from the 1970s onward show wives simply not following husbands. American women's votes moved away from their men, their pastors, and their party machines, precisely because gender-rights questions made the ballot a matter of individual conscience. The gender gap, in other words, was never a demographic accident. It was the electoral shadow of women's independence. Dearborn, Hamtramck, Minneapolis, Columbus Which brings us to 2024's most under examined story: how Muslim American communities in the Midwest voted, and how they were mobilized. Michigan. Dearborn -- the capital of Arab America -- flipped, going Trump 42 percent, Harris 36, Jill Stein 18, according to the New York Times. Hamtramck, the only Muslim-run city in America, went hard for Trump. Its mayor, Amer Ghalib, became the first Muslim or Arab-American official to endorse Trump, and was later named a White House adviser on Arab-American affairs. The "Abandon Harris" campaign delivered its message from the Friday-prayer pulpit at the American Muslim Center in Dearborn, while the advocacy group Emgage campaigned for Harris -- an intra-community fight playing out in religious space. Nationally, CAIR's exit poll of 1,575 verified Muslim voters found Stein 53 percent, Trump 21, Harris 20: a seismic break from a half-century of Democratic alignment, driven overwhelmingly by Gaza. Minnesota. The Somali community of Minneapolis -- the heart of Ilhan Omar's district -- was heavily mobilized through mosque and community networks, torn between Harris, Trump, and third parties, as the Sahan Journal documented. The community's new salience produced a train of viral controversies: a state election official's Somali-language TV message that ignited an integrity row; conservative influencers staging niqab-clad "voter fraud" stunts at polling places that ended with a criminal probe -- of the influencers, not the voters. The Washington Post fact-checked the "widespread illegal Somali voting" allegations as false, or at least unproven. Ohio. Columbus holds one of the country's largest Somali communities. Viral clips alleging translators or elders steering voters circulated in 2024 and after, but no mainstream reporting substantiated systematic directed balloting there. Running underneath all of it was a repeated claim on social media: that imams told men their wives' votes would follow theirs, that husbands carried the household ballot, that these communities voted as blocs under male instruction. The documented reality is more interesting than the rumor -- and in one structural sense, the rumor's critics and its believers can both claim a piece of it. The Structure Was Mars. The Votes Weren 't. What is true: in Dearborn, Hamtramck, Minneapolis, and Columbus, votes were organized through male-led institutions -- imams, male mayors, mosque networks, male-led campaigns like Abandon Harris. Bloc endorsement, pulpit mobilization, community discipline. That is a genuinely different mobilization structure from 1972-1982 America, when women's votes were organized outside male clerical authority and broke from male voters. Anyone who wants to see a contrast with the Roe and ERA era has a real one to point at: single-issue communal politics brokered through the mosque as political machine, versus the autonomous women's politics American women built for themselves after they won the vote. What is not true -- or at least not supported by the best data we have -- is the strong version: that the women voted as the men asked. ISPU's American Muslim Poll 2025, the most careful post-election look at the community, found that 42 percent of Muslim men voted for Trump, against just 17 percent of Muslim women. That is a twenty-five-point gender gap inside the community -- two and a half times the national gender gap. Muslim women did not follow the men into Trump. They split from them even harder than American women split from American men, and stayed overwhelmingly anti-Trump while the men surged. The community's internal divisions ran along lines -- race, class, generation -- that had nothing to do with male direction: nearly half of white Muslims voted Trump; Black Muslims stayed heavily Democratic. Two years later, with governor's mansions and statehouses at stake instead of the presidency, the National Exit Poll put Muslim voters at 87 percent Democratic, and CAIR's exit survey found the community had "overwhelmingly backed Democrats" -- men and women alike, converging on the same slates: Jocelyn Benson for governor and Abdul El-Sayed for Senate in Michigan, where El-Sayed carried Dearborn by sixty-five points on the highest turnout in the city's recorded history, and a record bench of Muslim women down the ballot -- Ilhan Omar re-elected by widening margins, Zaynab Mohamed in Minnesota, Munira Abdullahi in Ohio. The 2024 gulf between Muslim men and Muslim women shrank to something pollsters could no longer cleanly measure. Whether one reads that as women voting in line with their community's men, or as men streaming back to the column the women had never left -- the likelier reading, since women were already more than eight in ten anti-Trump in 2024 -- the Mars-and-Venus fact is the same: inside this community, the gender gap existed only for as long as Trump's own name was on the ballot. Take him off, and the two planets were suddenly standing in the same polling booth, marking the same ovals. | | ---|---|--- So the 2024 Midwest story is not "men told women how to vote." It is: men moved drastically on a foreign-policy issue through institutions men lead, and women -- starting from the same pews -- refused to move nearly as far. The Point, Stated Plainly 1\. Gray's thesis got its best-ever empirical support in 2024. Men and women voted at opposite poles nationally -- ten points apart, majorities on opposite sides -- and roughly thirty points apart among the young. That is a complete inversion of the pre-1960s pattern, when women were the more conservative bloc and the sexes voted alike. 2\. The inversion was manufactured by the Roe and ERA realignment, and its engine was women's independence from male-led institutions. Every gender gap since 1980 is the residue of that independence. 3\. The Muslim-community vote in Michigan, Minnesota, and Ohio is the mirror image in structure: ballots brokered through male-led religious and municipal institutions around a single issue. Yet even there, the women broke from the men -- by twenty-five points. Gray's Venus survives even where the mobilization structure looks like Mars. Gray's book is not social science, and a gap is an average that no individual voter owes anyone. And the viral claims of directed voting were mostly unverified or outright fabricated stunts; the documented story is communal bloc politics plus an enormous intra-community gender split -- not proof that Muslim women voted on their husbands' instructions. The deeper irony is worth closing on. The Roe and ERA era taught America that women's votes diverge from men's when women claim their own ballots. 2024 suggests the divergence is now permanent -- ten points nationally, thirty among the young, twenty-five inside a community where no one predicted it. Mars and Venus are not communicating better. They are voting further apart than at any time since women first entered the electorate -- and the one place where men's votes and women's votes most nearly converged last November was the place where men's institutions did the most organizing. Sources : Edison Research exit polls via Rutgers CAWP and the Roper Center; Pew Research Center validated-voter study (2025); Tufts CIRCLE youth exit-poll analysis; New York Times (Dearborn results); BBC News (Abandon Harris, Dearborn); Al Jazeera (Amer Ghalib endorsement); CAIR 2024 national exit poll; ISPU American Muslim Poll 2025; Sahan Journal (Minnesota Muslims); Washington Post fact-check on Somali voting allegations.
