| | Thanksgiving is a time to reflect on what we are grateful for, spend time with loved ones, and look out for our neighbors. But as families across Northwest Washington prepare to gather around the table, many of our neighbors are struggling to put food on theirs. **Over the past year, rising grocery prices and cuts to federal nutrition programs have created real challenges for families across Northwest Washington.** I have heard from local food bank volunteers, employees, and community leaders about the growing demand for food assistance and the challenges they face meeting that need. Our local food banks and community organizations continue to step up to help families put food on the table. But they cannot do it alone. **This Thanksgiving, I want to share a few resources for anyone who needs assistance or wants to lend a helping hand.** **_If you or someone you know needs food assistance:_** There are food banks and community organizations throughout Northwest Washington providing groceries, meals, and other essential services to families in need. [**You can use the Washington 211 resource directory to find food banks, meal programs, and other assistance near you.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144049410/662246475/-270235867?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODIxN2U3NS1mNWU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzMxOWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0BKVXdQsWDZkN6-Eq4st_uk2Yf2eKfHDtKD-oy2YZh8=&emci=3057bb91-dbe8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&emdi=08217e75-f5e8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&ceid=9494239) [FIND FOOD ASSISTANCE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144049411/662246476/-270235867?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODIxN2U3NS1mNWU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzMxOWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0BKVXdQsWDZkN6-Eq4st_uk2Yf2eKfHDtKD-oy2YZh8=&emci=3057bb91-dbe8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&emdi=08217e75-f5e8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&ceid=9494239) **_If you are looking for ways to give back:_** Our local food banks rely on volunteers, donations, and community support to serve our neighbors. Whether you can donate food, contribute financially, or volunteer your time, every effort makes a difference. Here are a few organizations serving communities across Northwest Washington:
* **Island and San Juan Counties:**[**Opportunity Council**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144049412/662246477/-361035232?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODIxN2U3NS1mNWU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzMxOWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0BKVXdQsWDZkN6-Eq4st_uk2Yf2eKfHDtKD-oy2YZh8=&emci=3057bb91-dbe8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&emdi=08217e75-f5e8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&ceid=9494239) — connects families with food assistance and other essential resources.
* **Skagit County:**[**Community Action of Skagit County**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144049413/662246478/1475027630?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODIxN2U3NS1mNWU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzMxOWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0BKVXdQsWDZkN6-Eq4st_uk2Yf2eKfHDtKD-oy2YZh8=&emci=3057bb91-dbe8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&emdi=08217e75-f5e8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&ceid=9494239) — connects residents with local food banks and food assistance programs.
* **Snohomish County:**[**Volunteers of America Western Washington**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144049414/662246479/-264129190?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODIxN2U3NS1mNWU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzMxOWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0BKVXdQsWDZkN6-Eq4st_uk2Yf2eKfHDtKD-oy2YZh8=&emci=3057bb91-dbe8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&emdi=08217e75-f5e8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&ceid=9494239)— provides hunger prevention services and other community support.
* **Whatcom County:**[**Bellingham Food Bank**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144049415/662246480/-523692251?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODIxN2U3NS1mNWU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzMxOWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0BKVXdQsWDZkN6-Eq4st_uk2Yf2eKfHDtKD-oy2YZh8=&emci=3057bb91-dbe8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&emdi=08217e75-f5e8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&ceid=9494239) — provides food assistance to individuals and families facing food insecurity.

You can also find additional food banks and meal programs throughout Washington through [**Food Lifeline**.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144049416/662246481/-11435254?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODIxN2U3NS1mNWU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzMxOWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0BKVXdQsWDZkN6-Eq4st_uk2Yf2eKfHDtKD-oy2YZh8=&emci=3057bb91-dbe8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&emdi=08217e75-f5e8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&ceid=9494239) **We all have a role to play in building stronger communities. Whether through volunteering, donating to an impactful charity, or simply lending a helping hand — your actions can uplift your neighborhood.** Thank you for being a part of my journey this year and for all you do to make Northwest Washington a great place to live. **Wishing you and your loved ones a Thanksgiving filled with warmth, gratitude, and joy.** With heartfelt thanks, _Rick_ | Express Donate: If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Rick Larsen instantly:

clean_body: Find local food assistance and ways to support Northwest Washington families this holiday season. | | | | Thanksgiving is a time to reflect on what we are grateful for, spend time with loved ones, and look out for our neighbors. But as families across Northwest Washington prepare to gather around the table, many of our neighbors are struggling to put food on theirs. Over the past year, rising grocery prices and cuts to federal nutrition programs have created real challenges for families across Northwest Washington. I have heard from local food bank volunteers, employees, and community leaders about the growing demand for food assistance and the challenges they face meeting that need. Our local food banks and community organizations continue to step up to help families put food on the table. But they cannot do it alone. This Thanksgiving, I want to share a few resources for anyone who needs assistance or wants to lend a helping hand. If you or someone you know needs food assistance: There are food banks and community organizations throughout Northwest Washington providing groceries, meals, and other essential services to families in need. If you are looking for ways to give back: Our local food banks rely on volunteers, donations, and community support to serve our neighbors. Whether you can donate food, contribute financially, or volunteer your time, every effort makes a difference. Here are a few organizations serving communities across Northwest Washington: Island and San Juan Counties: — connects families with food assistance and other essential resources. Skagit County: — connects residents with local food banks and food assistance programs. Snohomish County:— provides hunger prevention services and other community support. Whatcom County: — provides food assistance to individuals and families facing food insecurity. You can also find additional food banks and meal programs throughout Washington through We all have a role to play in building stronger communities. Whether through volunteering, donating to an impactful charity, or simply lending a helping hand — your actions can uplift your neighborhood. Thank you for being a part of my journey this year and for all you do to make Northwest Washington a great place to live. Wishing you and your loved ones a Thanksgiving filled with warmth, gratitude, and joy. Friend, With Thanksgiving just around the corner, I want to personally thank you for all the support you’ve given me since I announced my reelection campaign. This year has been full of challenges for everyone. We watched as the Trump administration stoked fear in our communities by sending ICE agents to our district. We saw so many families here in Central and Southern Illinois impacted by unnecessary wars, high grocery costs and energy bills, and tariffs that only benefited the wealthy and Trump himself. But I’ve also seen hope for a better future. Everywhere I went across IL-13, so many of you reached out to me and my team about the changes you want to see right now. As a result, you and millions of Americans voted for a Democratic majority to lower costs and keep this administration to check. **And as the new Chair of the New Dems Coalition, Americans in red and purple areas are taking charge for a more affordable country – which is both inspiring and exciting to see.** None of this would have been possible without your support – and I am so thankful to keep serving you in Congress. So from my family to yours, I wish you a happy and relaxing Thanksgiving. Thank you, Nikki

clean_body: Use your OR PTC before the end of the year!| | | Peter, It’s the season of gratitude and we have a lot to be grateful about here at OLCV. Thanks to supporters like you, earlier this month we re-elected Governor Tina Kotek and added to our pro-environment majorities in both chambers of the Oregon House and Senate. These wins wouldn’t be possible without you. Eligible Oregonians can give $50 (individual) or $100 (couple filing jointly) to the OLCV PAC and get it back when they file their taxes. You are eligible if: You are an Oregon resident. You will submit an Oregon tax return this year. You make less than $75,000 (individual) or $150,000 (married couple filing jointly). You must use your Political Tax Credit before midnight on December 31st, or you’ll miss out! Our 2026 Primary and General Election wins set us up to accomplish big things in 2027, like passing important legislation to help us meet our climate goals, hold data centers accountable, phase out toxic chemicals in everyday household products, and protect our water. You can help by donating to OLCV using your Political Tax Credit to ensure we have the resources we need to continue electing pro-environment candidates and protecting Oregon’s natural legacy. body:
Back from orientation, grateful for this team, and ready to get to work. | |
Peter, **Now that I’m back from two weeks of freshman orientation in Washington, I’m able to take a breath and say thank you.** Through every up and down of this campaign, you kept showing up. You believed in making government a positive force in people’s lives again, so people can survive and thrive and have hope for the future. That’s what this work is about. At orientation, I met a nurse practitioner who spent hours trying to get AI-driven denials of her patients’ care overturned, and a fellow LGBTQ state legislator who flipped a deeply Republican district. These are the people I’ll be serving alongside. We’re already talking about how to deliver, and I came home excited to get to work. The freshman class makes up about a quarter of the House and we’re going to shake things up. We’re going to deliver on the things we promised – like campaign finance reform, a ban on stock trading, committee chair term limits. We know we’re pushing the envelope – that’s why you elected us. This is the most diverse House Democratic leadership in history. The first Black speaker in U.S. history, a woman majority leader, a Latino whip, a Chinese American caucus chair, the first trans member of leadership (_take that, Nancy Mace!_) and many more! I ran for Congress to lower the cost of living, protect access to health care, and stand up to Donald Trump and his administration when they threaten our communities and our fundamental rights. You helped get me here. Now I'm getting ready to return to Congress as part of a new Democratic majority.

clean_body: This November we defended it against everything Republicans threw our way. | | | | = | | | | I've spent a lot of time since Election Day thinking about how far we've come. Two years ago we flipped this seat. This November we defended it against everything Republicans threw our way. Now I'm getting ready to return to Congress as part of a new Democratic majority. I'm excited about what we can accomplish. We have an opportunity to focus on lowering costs, making life easier for families across the country and holding the Trump administration accountable. That's what I want to spend my time doing. But I also know how hard we had to fight to get here. Republicans made it clear just how badly they wanted this seat and I don't expect them to suddenly give up. Peter, On Monday, I joined Clark County Commissioner William McCurdy II in Las Vegas to hand out hundreds of Thanksgiving turkeys for the fourth year in a row. Being able to provide families with Thanksgiving dinner has become one of my favorite traditions. At a time when so many families across America are struggling with rising costs, the holidays can bring added stress. No one should have to choose between putting Thanksgiving dinner on the table or keeping the lights on. **And when a neighbor is worried about making ends meet, showing up can make a real difference.** No matter our politics or disagreements, we are bound together by a shared belief in community, dignity, and taking care of each other. I’m grateful to everyone who cooked a meal, packed a bag of groceries, or took time out of a busy week to lend a hand. I hope this holiday gives you a chance to spend time with the people you love and to check in on someone who could use a hand. From my family to yours, Happy Thanksgiving. Onward,
Ro

# [Hot PCE locks December hike as AI stocks crater](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nasdaq futures sank nearly 3% and selling widened after the open as October Personal Consumption Expenditure **[held at 3.8% headline](https://substack.com/redirect/8b591285-6f6c-4eb1-bf64-c006a09a2eaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and core printed a tick hot at 3.3%, locking in expectations for a quarter-point Fed increase on Dec. 9.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Hot PCE print** : Headline personal-consumption expenditures rose 3.8% year-over-year while core accelerated to 3.3%, above the 3.2% consensus and the highest core since November 2023.
* **Futures plunge** : Overnight Nasdaq 100 futures dropped as much as 3.1% and S&P 500 futures fell near 2% before the data hit.
* **Selling widens** : Early Wednesday trade pushed the Nasdaq down 3.7%, the S&P 500 down 2.6% and the Dow down more than 800 points as losses spread beyond chips.
* **Tariff overlay** : Fresh Section 301 proposals on 14 trading partners added to pressure on tech and growth names into the Thanksgiving break.

# [Huang's Nvidia comeback fades into therapy and a stock drop](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Jensen Huang's Monday reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has **[already given way to another selloff](https://substack.com/redirect/305859c8-dfa3-4762-be3e-01f30003106c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , with the executive telling staff he is in daily therapy and apologizing while lawmakers schedule December hearings and the shares fall further.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Therapy and apology** : At a Tuesday all-hands, Huang said he spends 90 minutes a day in therapy, apologized for code-of-conduct breaches, and disclosed additional affairs to the board before his return.
* **No succession plan** : He told employees a formal successor would create unnecessary hierarchy, leaving Nvidia without a designated backup after his 11-day exit.
* **Congress schedule** : Private interviews with three House committees are set for Dec. 1 and a public Senate Banking hearing for Dec. 3 on chip exports and the reported ties.
* **Trump comments** : The president said a pardon is always an option and it is not too late for a U.S. stake, while disclosure filings show he holds Nvidia shares worth tens of millions.

# [Jury convicts Huawei on Iran sanctions, fraud and trade secrets](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A Brooklyn **[federal jury convicted Huawei](https://substack.com/redirect/9b8e831c-5b8d-4ceb-862c-22dd93384333?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and three subsidiaries on 10 of 12 counts, including conspiracy to steal U.S. trade secrets, bank and wire fraud, and Iran sanctions violations, while acquitting the company of racketeering.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Mixed verdict** : Jurors found the Chinese tech giant guilty on the trade-secret, fraud and sanctions charges but cleared it of the racketeering conspiracy that would have labeled it a criminal enterprise.
* **Trial length** : The verdict followed a three-month trial; Huawei said the conviction lacked legal or factual merit and signaled it would pursue further legal action.
* **Iran links** : Prosecutors alleged a two-decade scheme that included lying to banks about work with Iran.
* **China response** : The company has rejected the outcome and indicated it will contest the findings.

# [Trump proposes new tariffs on China, EU and 12 others](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The U.S. Trade Representative unveiled proposed Section 301 duties on[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/11c37f78-596c-4730-a739-983677539d45?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[14 trading partners after an excess-capacity probe,](https://substack.com/redirect/11c37f78-596c-4730-a739-983677539d45?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/11c37f78-596c-4730-a739-983677539d45?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)with China facing an additional 20% rate and several others at 15%, a move that added to Wednesday's futures pressure.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Scope of probe** : The investigation covers China, the European Union, Japan, South Korea, India, Vietnam and others, with higher rates possibly taking effect in January.
* **China rate** : The proposal layers a 20% duty on China atop existing measures, with a higher 40% rate possible if talks collapse.
* **Market reaction** : The announcement hit Nasdaq futures and Nvidia shares as investors digested another potential tariff round.
* **Truce context** : The timing comes as Washington and Beijing weigh whether to extend their current trade arrangement.

# [Dell AI servers boom but stock still falls hard](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Dell reported **[third-quarter revenue that more than doubled](https://substack.com/redirect/9337fc4c-5174-46bb-b567-5424c367e004?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on AI server demand, raised its full-year outlook to $202 billion, and expanded its buyback by $25 billion, yet the shares dropped in premarket trade as the sector sold off.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Revenue jump** : Sales reached $54.94 billion with adjusted earnings of $9.45 a share, both ahead of estimates, driven by infrastructure demand.
* **Raised guide** : The company lifted its fiscal-year revenue outlook to $202 billion and authorized an additional $25 billion in share repurchases.
* **AI orders** : Management pointed to a large AI server backlog and continued hyperscaler demand even as the stock moved lower.
* **Timing issue** : The beat arrived on a day of broad tech selling, with Dell down alongside Nvidia and other AI-linked names.

# [Thanksgiving dinner hits $58.63 as turkey jumps 10%](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The American Institute for Economic Research's 2026 Thanksgiving Cost Index rose[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/33fe11be-98a8-43d4-8df1-780cde67eabf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[2.6% from a year earlier and 32.1% above 2019](https://substack.com/redirect/33fe11be-98a8-43d4-8df1-780cde67eabf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** levels to a record, led by an 8.4% jump in turkey and poultry prices amid avian flu and higher diesel costs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Index rise** : The AIER measure reached an all-time high, with turkey and poultry the largest contributors to the year-over-year increase.
* **Drivers** : Avian flu outbreaks and elevated diesel costs pushed the poultry component higher.
* **Longer view** : The index stands 32.1% above its 2019 level.
* **Consumer impact** : The record reading arrives as households prepare for the holiday amid broader price pressures.

# [Oil falls as surplus fears overpower Middle East risks](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Crude prices declined as traders[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/af583965-7748-4cb0-8285-f188416c7f4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[weighed a prospective global supply surplus](https://substack.com/redirect/af583965-7748-4cb0-8285-f188416c7f4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/af583965-7748-4cb0-8285-f188416c7f4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)ahead of an OPEC+ meeting this weekend against renewed Saudi-Houthi hostilities that raised concerns about Red Sea shipping.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Supply outlook** : Falling prices reflected expectations of rising production and a looming surplus, with Brent holding near $90 despite geopolitical risks.
* **Middle East factor** : Renewed attacks and tensions in the region failed to offset the downward pressure from supply assessments.
* **OPEC+ timing** : The moves came ahead of the group's weekend meeting, with Iraq separately rejecting an assessment that its sustainable capacity is under 5 million barrels a day.
* **Product demand** : Soft refined-product demand added to the pressure even as shipping concerns persisted around Hormuz and the Red Sea.

# [Consumer confidence jumps to 103.3 after midterms](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Conference Board's **[consumer-confidence index rose to 103.3](https://substack.com/redirect/8ab0dc94-2318-41fc-aeff-863f0ee6e734?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in November, far above the 92.2 forecast and the highest since January 2025, with sharp gains in both current conditions and near-term outlooks following the midterms.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ecda1d4c-a278-44a2-b6da-09b5f31ec7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Index jump** : The headline measure increased roughly 11 points, marking the biggest two-month rebound since the COVID vaccine period.
* **Labor views** : Improvement was led by a sharp rise in assessments of the job market, with gas prices below $4 a gallon also cited as a factor.
* **Analyst skepticism** : Some researchers dismissed the rebound as having limited predictive value for actual spending, calling the survey unreliable.
* **Timing** : The release came Tuesday as markets digested mixed equity moves and ahead of the Wednesday inflation data.

This Thanksgiving we take a moment to hone in on what we’re really thankful for: you. We have a rare opportunity over the next few months for big, bold, transformational change out of Harrisburg with the incoming trifecta. Even in the face of MAGA billionaires like Elon Musk and Jeffrey Yass, we put in the work and the people prevailed knocking on 60,000 doors in districts where incumbent Republicans lost. This win was a labor of love spanning years of political education and mobilization in Pennsylvania’s working class communities. For now, we hope you are able to spend this Thanksgiving with good people and good health. Rest up because organizing is a year-round effort and we’ll be reaching out to have you join us for what’s next. Cheers,
One PA Action Team
---
| One PA is a grassroots movement for racial, economic, and social justice in Pennsylvania. We empower Black communities through voter education, endorse candidates who share our values, and prioritize leadership development. Our commitment is to challenge political disillusionment, protect and expand democracy, and unite everyday people to have a voice in our political system.

I have a PhD in clinical psychology, which allows me to see my family clearly – and it’s clear that Donald is a textbook narcissist. He has always felt that his needs and desires come above everyone else – that’s why he directed his supporters to the Capitol on January 6th, why he’s plastering his name on everything he can, and why he’s threatening to steal this November’s election. His supporters enable this narcissism, but nothing bruises a narcissist’s ego like people who refuse to be intimidated by them. Zoe Lofgren is one of those people who will not be intimidated by my uncle or any of the small men and women who serve his narcissistic desires. **That’s why I was proud to endorse her re-election campaign. ** Zoe has been in the room for every presidential impeachment of my lifetime. She was a young Judiciary Committee staffer during Nixon's impeachment. She sat on that same committee for Clinton's impeachment. Donald has since called for the members of that committee to be prosecuted. Zoe has never blinked once. That is what actual strength looks like.
It’s no secret that the GOP is terrified right now. Donald’s approval rating is tanking, and he’s bringing the whole party down with him.

# WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 25, 2026
---
**
Dear Reader,**

With the end of the year almost here, I'm writing with a personal ask.

Nobody knows what comes next. Things are shifting in Washington, and statehouses across the country are rewriting the rules. Markets are swinging, and the financial ground under everyday Americans feels less steady every week. At a time like this, what you need most is information you can trust.

That kind of information is disappearing.

Media companies across the country keep going bankrupt. Some made bad business decisions. Some traded facts for partisan spin. Some never figured out the internet. When they fail, they leave a gap.

So ask yourself: **who 's going to fill it?
**
Can you rely on CNN for unbiased news? The New York Times? Facebook's algorithm?

You know the answer.

**You can rely on _The Flyover_.** For almost four years you've trusted us to shoot straight. No spin, no agenda, just the facts every morning. Millions of Americans now feel the same way:
* **Over 7 million readers** get _The Flyover_ every day
* **12 state editions** cover the news closest to home
* **Our podcast** reaches millions of listeners every month

I’ve spent the week trying to find a better word than “grateful.” There isn’t one. So grateful will have to do — as a start. This year, millions of people said loudly and clearly that we deserve better. They stood up for their neighbors and for the most vulnerable among us. They reached across disagreement to find common ground. I’m proud of every bit of it. And yes, grateful. Now it’s on Democrats to earn the trust voters just placed in us. I’m ready. My team and I are already at work on legislation for the new Congress, and I’ll have more to share soon. For now, I’m taking a short break like everyone else, and I’m heading straight for the sweet potato casserole. I hope you get some time this week with the people you love, a plate of your own favorite food, and a moment to take in how far we’ve come. Happy Thanksgiving. —Sara P.S. Here’s the recipe my mom and I use for our go-to sweet potato casserole!
---
_Ruth’s Chris Sweet Potato Casserole Recipe:_
\- 3/4 cup brown sugar
\- 1/4 cup flour
\- 3/4 cup chopped nuts (pecans preferred)
\- 1/4 cup melted butter
\- 3/4 cup sugar
\- 1/4 teaspoon salt
\- 1/4 teaspoon vanilla
\- 2 cups mashed sweet potatoes
\- 1 egg, well beaten
\- 1/4 cup butter Process:
1\. Combine crust mixture in mixing bowl and put to one side.
2\. Combine sweet potato mixture ingredients in a mixing bowl in the order listed. Combine thoroughly.
3\. Pour sweet potato mixture into buttered baking dish
4\. Sprinkle crust mixture evenly onto surface of sweet potato mixture.
5\. Bake for 30 minutes at 350°. Allow to set for at least 30 minutes before serving.

| | | Being a parent is hard enough without having to worry about whether the diapers you put on your kid are safe. This week, I led a bipartisan effort calling on the Consumer Product Safety Commission to recall Millie Moon diapers following hundreds of reports of painful rashes, blistering, and chemical burns in babies. We're demanding answers about the materials used in these diapers, how they're manufactured, and what steps are being taken to ensure they're safe. The company maintains that its products have passed independent testing, but parents deserve answers about the injuries being reported. This isn't the first time I've led on an issue like this. Remember when parents were driving from grocery store to grocery store just to find baby formula? Last year, I secured an amendment in the House Appropriations Committee to investigate corporate consolidation in the infant formula industry and identify ways to increase competition. I've also been working to rebuild our domestic pulp and paper industry, protect your right to repair the things you own, crack down on shrinkflation, and require manufacturers to tell you how long the appliances you're buying are actually expected to last. These issues might seem unrelated, but they're rooted in a lot of the same questions: where our goods are made, who controls their production, and what protections consumers have when something goes wrong. Whether it’s the diapers you put on your kid, the formula you feed them, or the appliances you spend your hard-earned money on, you ought to know that what you’re buying is safe, that it works, and that the companies making it can be held accountable when something goes wrong. **[Will you make a contribution today to help me keep fighting for families across the district?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144055752/662265532/-995582223?refcode=261123-recall&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3ZTliZmQ0MS0wNWU5LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzMxOWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sCDJIMp7y3pmH6ZUpwBEnzvgvXAZEZElqvYZVEuNf5w=)**

body:
When Antifa attackers beat Andy Ngo, we took his case and won.

Friend,
---
| | | My name is Mark Trammell. I lead the **Center for American Liberty.**

We're a nonprofit law firm. We defend Americans who are being silenced, pushed out, and left to fight alone.

This time of year, a lot of people think about giving. Let me tell you a story about why giving matters.

**It 's about my friend Andy Ngo.**

---
You may have seen Andy on Fox News. He has testified before Congress and spoken at the White House about Antifa and the violent far Left.

In 2019, Andy was in Portland covering Antifa when a mob attacked him.

They beat him. He ended up in the hospital with bleeding in his brain.

Plenty of groups wouldn't touch his case. Too controversial. Too risky.

**The Center for American Liberty took it anyway. **

**And we won**.A court ordered three of his attackers to pay $300,000.
---
[ **Yes, Double My Gift**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckbGO2zAMhp9G3s6waEtxBg8FggAdrijQoaNAU0xMVLJci77i3r7IXcZOXfn__D4Q_PkaXlGSrPdvmHmSWsNegy78vh26SJZVF15K3UQxBejAv1j7Ai4gqbxxGLCJkwM73saGJ3s6O9-7DlyzTBhHT-hmP55nQgcMbkSYiSwwR5gbmR48a8HZc9_B0NI488lavLF31p9HM3THFlG5lbVK5EqlbFtJokK1Lfu9SdOiulXTfzFwNXDFlWPRNsnMu74Tr8r7o2jgSjdM4RlkVFo-rglIv01_reXYiQOVyKa_fP3x3frBDdaAPzSHzFGObPoLZ5T0HH6umP6y4B6x_vogfUaEeUO5r6a__Nv67CnvD2qzT3H7IylJ9SczdPeHpaWSG_2vh7xN8DcAAP__xzie7A)
---

We're not afraid to file lawsuits in the toughest places in the country. Portland was one of them.

Today, we're fighting for parents in Colorado and California who were kept in the dark by their children's schools.

And we represent Chloe Cole in her landmark lawsuit against the doctors and hospital involved in the medical transition she underwent as a minor.

**These fights take real resources. And we can 't win them without people like you. **

That's why I'm so excited to share this with you, Friend,. Thanks to a generous donor, we were able to activate the**$25,000 Liberty Defense Match. **

Every gift made before midnight on December 18 will be **DOUBLED, dollar for dollar. **

And when you give $50 or more, we'll send you a copy of Andy's new book, _The Zizians: Inside a Trans Death Cult_.

subject: Beyond grateful
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTQxMjIxNjAS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjU4MDEyNTkyNAS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Peter, It’s been an incredible week — and we couldn’t have achieved these historic
victories without you. Together with our state affiliates, we helped elect pro-climate majorities in
the U.S. House and Senate, secured new pro-clean energy trifecta governments in
six states (and counting!), and helped elect climate and democracy champions at
every level of government across the country. Thank you. These decisive victories are a resounding rejection of Trump’s dirty energy
policies, which are enriching Big Oil and corporate CEOs at our expense. Voters across the country made it clear that they’re fed up with Trump and MAGA
Republican policies jacking up their energy bills, dirty data centers polluting
their communities, and corporate corruption being allowed to run rampant. We listened to these voters, we strategized, and we got to work. With your support, LCV Victory Fund and affiliated entities launched electoral
programs that harnessed voters’ anger over Trump’s failed energy policies,
provided them with clear solutions, and transformed their desire for change into
action. While some races have yet be called, thanks to supporters like you, we were able
to: Win in 29 races to secure a pro-clean energy, pro-democracy majority in the U.S. House.Protect and pick up seven seats in the U.S. Senate, helping climate champions win in IA, ME, MI, NC, NH, OH, and TX and flipping the chamber.Elect 18 governors, including three who flipped their state’s governor’s mansion from red to blue.Secure six new pro-clean energy, pro-democracy state legislative majorities (so far).Win seats on local and state utility boards, state Supreme Courts, and other offices that have an outsized impact on clean energy and climate policy, including an outright majority on the Georgia Public Service Commission to control energy policy in the state.Defeat every single anti-environment candidate on our Dirty Dozen list https://links.messages.lcv.. And this is just the beginning. LCV is ready to tackle high utility bills by advancing clean, affordable energy;
rein in polluting data centers; and bring a pro-climate, pro-democracy agenda to
state capitols and Washington, D.C. We couldn’t have reached this pivotal moment without you, Peter. I’m so
excited for what comes next. With fierce commitment, Pete Maysmith

President

Congress. Our 2026 New Member Guide https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/_ is up on our website and will continue to be updated. This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. name: OnePA Team
subject: Tell Congress to stop the SNAP cost shift before they leave for the year
body:
Congress can still stop the SNAP cost shift to states in its year-end spending package. Tell your lawmakers to protect SNAP before they leave for the year. | |
---
Peter, Tomorrow, families across Pennsylvania and the country will sit down for Thanksgiving dinner, and for a lot of our neighbors, the food on that table depends on SNAP. **More than 5 million people across the country have already lost access to SNAP since Congress passed Trump’s Big Brutal Bill in July 2025.** That same law is now pushing the cost of running SNAP onto the states, and the program was never meant to run this way. As of October, the federal government covers just 25% of SNAP's administrative costs, down from 50% -- that means states are stuck with the other 75%. Starting in October 2027, most states with SNAP payment error rates of 6% or higher will have to pay at least 5% of the benefits families use to buy groceries, up to 15%. It will be the first time in history the federal government has not covered the full cost of SNAP benefits. **Trump and congressional Republicans made this choice on purpose, because they knew our families would be the ones to pay for it.** USDA estimates Pennsylvania will have to spend $138.3 million more each year on SNAP administrative costs, and our state budget covered about $116 million of that on an annual basis. Nationwide, states have budgeted $469 million less than USDA says they need. **Congress can still prevent this harm in its year-end spending package** , one of the must-pass bills lawmakers will take up before they leave for the year. **When thousands of us flood our representatives and senators with letters at once, protecting SNAP becomes much harder for them to leave on the cutting room floor.** [**Tell your representative and senators to protect SNAP in year-end legislation by stopping the SNAP cost shift to states and restoring the federal government's 50% share of the cost of running the Congress must eliminate the shift of SNAP benefit costs to states or, at a minimum, delay it for two years without cuts to SNAP in future years. Lawmakers must also restore the federal government's share of the cost of running SNAP, so states are never forced to choose between feeding families and funding everything else in their budgets.
**If states cut back on SNAP or walk away from it altogether, the people who lose the most are children, older adults, veterans, and people with disabilities who count on the program to put food on the table.** Those are our neighbors, our families, and the people sitting next to us at Thanksgiving dinner.
The burden on states is already larger than USDA estimated, with many states unable to fully cover the funding gap. As state lawmakers write their next budgets, they could face a choice between paying these new costs and cutting other essential services, and some states could even consider leaving SNAP entirely.

name: Eric H. Holder, Jr.
subject: Have you had a moment to catch your breath?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE NATIONAL REDISTRICTING ACTION FUND
body:
Progress is not always permanent. Our march must continue.
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144059479/662269779/-453679381?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjAxMTQzNWJiLTA4ZTktZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzE5YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=a7qNETDvXbV50FCeZWVKf5erISA2XFxINP4Euch1kkE=&emci=6c4fbc50-f7e8-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&emdi=011435bb-08e9-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&ceid=8431045)

_Formerly All On The Line_

Have you had a moment to catch your breath, Peter?
It's been a few weeks, so I thought it was time to reflect on the lessons from this election cycle.
If nothing else, I believe the midterms were a testament to the fact that we — the people — have the power to protect democracy when we use that power at the ballot box.
**In spite of relentless attacks on fair elections, in spite of a Supreme Court determined to wipe away decades of progress on voting rights, in spite of politicians determined to scare people away from casting their ballots, the will of the people prevailed in this election.**
That's a victory for those of us who believe in representative democracy.
But like all victories in our system of government, there is no guarantee how long it will last, and that is why we must keep up the fight.
**Progress is not always permanent** — we saw that play out painfully when the Court gutted the Voting Rights Act, the crown jewel of the civil rights movement.
But it matters how we respond after setbacks. After the Courts’ disastrous ruling in _Louisiana v. Callais_ , people across the South refused to be counted out – they flexed their voting muscle and swung outcomes many didn't think were possible.
And it matters how we respond after we win — in that limited window in which we have a chance to push for generational change.
**It's time to go for it.** We need to undo the damage done by radical courts and anti-democracy lawmakers in states across the country. These are fights that aren’t won in one election cycle — just as the civil rights movement wasn't about one march or one protest or one landmark law.
But it's equally true that each one of us must seize the opportunity in front of us and do our part, to paraphrase Dr. King, to bend that arc of the moral universe toward justice.
That’s why we do this work. And I’m so grateful to be doing it alongside people like you, Peter.
**If you can, invest in this ongoing fight for a truly representative democracy by[making a recurring donation](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144059480/662269780/-1059218283?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_AGHolderPostElection_email_20261125-AOTL-Tier1-AGHolderPostElection_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20261125-AOTL-Tier1-AGHolderPostElection_&utm_campaign=AGHolderPostElection&recurring=1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjAxMTQzNWJiLTA4ZTktZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzE5YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=a7qNETDvXbV50FCeZWVKf5erISA2XFxINP4Euch1kkE=) — or just a [one-time gift](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144059481/662269781/-1059218283?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_AGHolderPostElection_email_20261125-AOTL-Tier1-AGHolderPostElection_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20261125-AOTL-Tier1-AGHolderPostElection_&utm_campaign=AGHolderPostElection&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjAxMTQzNWJiLTA4ZTktZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzE5YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=a7qNETDvXbV50FCeZWVKf5erISA2XFxINP4Euch1kkE=). **
**Let's lock arms, march forward, and bend that arc together.**
In solidarity,

clean_body: Progress is not always permanent. Our march must continue. | Formerly All On The Line Have you had a moment to catch your breath, Peter? It's been a few weeks, so I thought it was time to reflect on the lessons from this election cycle. If nothing else, I believe the midterms were a testament to the fact that we — the people — have the power to protect democracy when we use that power at the ballot box. In spite of relentless attacks on fair elections, in spite of a Supreme Court determined to wipe away decades of progress on voting rights, in spite of politicians determined to scare people away from casting their ballots, the will of the people prevailed in this election. That's a victory for those of us who believe in representative democracy. But like all victories in our system of government, there is no guarantee how long it will last, and that is why we must keep up the fight. Progress is not always permanent — we saw that play out painfully when the Court gutted the Voting Rights Act, the crown jewel of the civil rights movement. But it matters how we respond after setbacks. After the Courts’ disastrous ruling in Louisiana v. Callais , people across the South refused to be counted out – they flexed their voting muscle and swung outcomes many didn't think were possible. And it matters how we respond after we win — in that limited window in which we have a chance to push for generational change. It's time to go for it. We need to undo the damage done by radical courts and anti-democracy lawmakers in states across the country. These are fights that aren’t won in one election cycle — just as the civil rights movement wasn't about one march or one protest or one landmark law. But it's equally true that each one of us must seize the opportunity in front of us and do our part, to paraphrase Dr. King, to bend that arc of the moral universe toward justice. That’s why we do this work. And I’m so grateful to be doing it alongside people like you, Peter. If you can, invest in this ongoing fight for a truly representative democracy by= — or just a =. Let's lock arms, march forward, and bend that arc together. In solidarity, Eric H. Every vote was counted, and the people of Hampton Roads – not politicians nor billionaires – decided the outcome. **I’m grateful for the opportunity to serve.** I’ve been serving our country since I was 17 years old — this is what I do best. I can’t wait to tackle costs for Hampton Roads families, fight for our veterans, and protect the Chesapeake Bay for the next generation. Thank you for putting your trust in me. **I’m grateful for my family, my neighbors, and the incredible team we’ve built over the past year.** A battleground House race like ours takes a real toll, but I couldn’t ask for a better support system. | | | |

| |

---

| | | Friend,
---
The call blasted across the police radio: "We need backup--NOW!"Officers ran. Inside a tiny shack, they found two sisters. One was five years old; the other was twenty months - still a baby.**Both were tied by their ankles ... and hanging upside down from the roof.**I'll call them Ana and Lucia. Those are not their real names. But this is their true story.One officer reached for the baby first and began cutting her down.Ana was still hanging beside her, waiting.She didn't scream; she didn't kick or cry or fight the rope. She just watched.**To her, this was normal.**

Friend, I have heard many rescue stories since the movie _Sound of Freedom_ came out.**This is one I cannot shake.** Ana and Lucia had been hurt by the very adults who were supposed to protect them. Hurt in ways I cannot - will not - describe to you.The ropes had cut deep into their ankles. Those marks would become scars._But that day, everything changed._ SOMEONE noticed. SOMEONE made the call. And SOMEONE answered.The officers carried both girls out of that shack.They were placed in a safe home through our program partner, House Parent Project.**Now let me tell you what happened next.** For more than three years, their house parents have fed them, tucked them in, and prayed over them every night.They have watched Ana and Lucia heal... grow... and laugh.Both girls go to school now. And little by little, they have learned something no child should ever have to learn: **Hands are meant to protect. Not hurt.** Today, they are thriving.And Friend, here is the part that makes me want to drop to my knees in thanks...**A loving family has stepped forward to adopt them.** Both of them. _Together._ That family is going through the approval process right now.The scars around their ankles tell where they have been. But they will never determine where they are going.Soon, two little girls who once hung from the roof of a shack will walk through the front door of their forever home.

Friend, here is what I cannot stop thinking about: Ana didn't scream.She had learned that no one was coming - but she was wrong. is why Sound of Freedom Foundation exists: to stop the sale of God's children.Thanks to the unwavering support of concerned, caring people like you, we equip the rescue partners who go in when the call comes.And through House Parent Project, your support will help us give rescued children what Ana and Lucia found: SAFE homes, LOVING house parents, and trauma-informed CARE. Because rescue is only the beginning. A rope can be cut in a minute, but healing takes years. The Bible says, "God sets the lonely in families" (Psalm 68:6).I believe that with my whole heart. And now I get to watch Him do it for two little sisters. Ana and Lucia were found, but the next child is still waiting.Let's answer for her too.GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE. A senior War Department official who pledged to sell his stake in his family's defense consulting firm still owns between $1 million and $5 million in the company over a year after his confirmation, according to his financial disclosures.
The official, Michael Dodd, is the assistant secretary of war for critical technologies. His office writes the Pentagon's technology roadmaps, which lay out what technologies the military needs as well as plans and funding strategies to develop them. In a September 2026 [interview](https://substack.com/redirect/d4523a72-97ac-4859-8120-41e394c6a8a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), he said these responsibilities give him "significant influence on what the services procure."
The firm he founded, Dioltas, [helps companies](https://substack.com/redirect/0928a854-b0d5-42f5-ba4b-d12e8479fa5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) move "critical technology" through the Pentagon contracting process, "from first relationship to strategic partnership to funding." Dodd's wife, Melanie, was the registered agent and treasurer for Dioltas until November, and their son Keegan is its manager, according to government filings. The three of them are listed as the owners of Dioltas's office in Indiana, according to property records. (Their other son, Carson, works as a business analyst at the firm.)
Companies listed as Dioltas clients, according to his 2025 nominee [disclosure](https://substack.com/redirect/54ef421e-d654-4e51-a4a9-e8b22704079a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) report, have won Pentagon contracts or other funding worth up to $4.3 billion since September 2025, more than $100 million of it already committed. Most of that money, up to about $3.5 billion of it, was awarded to Dioltas's clients in contracts that the Pentagon solicited after Dodd was confirmed by the Senate that month. These clients include defense-technology firms ManTech International and JRC Integrated Systems, counter-drone company Allen Control Systems, and the microelectronics manufacturer SkyWater Technology. Drop Site News asked the firms if they were current clients of Dioltas, and whether Dioltas helped them win the Pentagon contracts awarded after Dodd's confirmation. None of the firms responded. Dodd himself did not respond to requests for comment.
The full list of Dioltas's current clients is not public.
Dodd is one of many federal [officials](https://substack.com/redirect/1b979051-69cb-441c-86a7-b5494573367d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with ties to [venture capital](https://substack.com/redirect/902d13f8-c585-4dcf-a824-79813cb947e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [private equity](https://substack.com/redirect/2d56016f-ce6c-41a1-88a2-f2aa27b9b835?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who have assumed [senior Pentagon posts](https://substack.com/redirect/bc702ebb-20fd-4af1-83a0-0860ec53ea75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the second Trump administration, as the department steers billions of dollars to new tech firms through fast-tracked contracts, often with limited oversight.
Dodd's apparent conflicts of interest are not exceptional. They reflect business as usual under President Donald Trump. From the [president](https://substack.com/redirect/ac04ad4b-8933-4231-a1e7-d23a014ff7f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on down, administration officials have regularly engaged in various forms of self-dealing. President Trump's second term is unique, according to many ethics experts, in its numerous officials' disregard for the separation between public duties and private interests.
Dodd worked as an advisor to "several prominent" venture capital funds with defense portfolios, according to his [official biography](https://substack.com/redirect/05beb46b-41ea-4d23-88ea-61c32cb16964?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and shepherded their companies through the Pentagon's acquisition process. He listed 8VC, a [top defense tech investor](https://substack.com/redirect/ee160f23-9924-4891-9188-03c34fe44bb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), as his sole business relationship aside from Dioltas in his 2025 Senate Armed Services Committee questionnaire. His [resume](https://substack.com/redirect/daf79efe-f83c-423f-95b3-3b7c97618876?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) shows that he began advising the firm in November 2024, but this work is not listed on his 2025 ethics disclosure. It is unclear when Dodd stopped advising 8VC.
Between November 2024 and Dodd's March 2025 nomination, 8VC portfolio firms received at least $100 million through deals with the Defense Innovation Unit, a Pentagon initiative with headquarters in Silicon Valley. The unit focuses on forging closer ties between the military and tech industry. At the same time that Dodd was advising 8VC, he held a senior position at the Defense Innovation Unit, where he developed its investment strategy and helped manage funding projects with defense-tech startups, according to his [official biography](https://substack.com/redirect/05beb46b-41ea-4d23-88ea-61c32cb16964?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The Defense Innovation Unit did not respond to Drop Site's questions about Dodd's role with 8VC.
8VC's founder and managing partner is Joe Lonsdale, a Palantir co-founder who is now helping shape the Pentagon's future tech priorities as a [participant](https://substack.com/redirect/2e1e7b10-272c-421e-93d1-869f97a7c982?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Project Meridian, a [controversial new initiative](https://substack.com/redirect/03e49cd4-64e7-4020-9c4d-68f4ff5e9bd0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that enlists defense-tech investors to advise the future of U.S. warfare. 8VC is a top investor in autonomous military tech firms Anduril--whose founder Palmer Luckey is Meridian's co-director--and Saronic, whose CEO Dino Mavrookas and [strategic advisor](https://substack.com/redirect/52f3ecb3-c30e-496f-81c0-238a67f279ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Gen. James Rainey are also Meridian panelists. Lonsdale has [argued](https://substack.com/redirect/e8f45529-a9c3-429a-a597-d56c014f161f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that new defense tech firms "need allies in government," and a nonprofit he controls has [lobbied](https://substack.com/redirect/ee160f23-9924-4891-9188-03c34fe44bb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Pentagon on defense contracting reform.
8VC's portfolio firms have done business in Dodd's [technology areas](https://substack.com/redirect/05beb46b-41ea-4d23-88ea-61c32cb16964?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). For example, Lonsdale co-founded Epirus, a defense contractor that creates directed-energy systems which has received around $30 million since Dodd took office. In September, Dodd said he would "[knuckle roll](https://substack.com/redirect/6ac972b9-e147-4323-be7d-5c1d50a44d11?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" military services to accelerate adoption of directed-energy technology.
8VC did not respond to Drop Site's questions about Dodd's involvement with the firm.
The Pentagon also did not answer Drop Site's questions about Dodd's relationship with Dioltas and other clients. A spokesperson for the War Department said, "The Department of War maintains a rigorous, multi-layered ethics framework that includes financial disclosure reviews, divestitures where appropriate, and screening to prevent conflicts of interest. Every DOW official, including Hon. Mike Dodd, is in full compliance with all ethical laws and regulations. Any claims otherwise are false."
Dioltas, in a response to an inquiry, said only, "We highly encourage you to check the facts."
## "At the Speed of Business"
In his May 2025 [ethics agreement](https://substack.com/redirect/acbcc781-6c0f-416a-bd35-a5da62707041?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Dodd pledged to resign from Dioltas "upon confirmation" and said that within 90 days of assuming his role at the Pentagon, he would divest his ownership in the company by selling his stake. He also said that his wife's role with the firm "will also end when my interest is sold." Those pledges do not appear to have been upheld.
The Senate confirmed Dodd on September 18, 2025. But he did not resign from Dioltas until September 2026, according to Indiana Secretary of State [records](https://substack.com/redirect/5a1ff5b0-2f68-440b-86b3-e331453c78c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). On the same day that he resigned from Dioltas, the records show, his wife took over as the firm's registered agent and his son Keegan became its manager. Two days after telling Drop Site to "check the facts," Dodd's son replaced his wife as registered agent, according to a federal disclosure filed on November 17.
Dodd still owns between $1 million and $5 million in Dioltas, according to his most recent annual financial disclosure, which he signed in May and which a government ethics lawyer formally approved in September. That disclosure also shows that, throughout 2025, he received $170,000 from Dioltas.
"There's a general prohibition on using public office for private gain," Virginia Canter, a former government ethics lawyer, told Drop Site. "I don't understand why DoD would allow him, as a Pentagon official, to retain a financial interest in a company whose business involves facilitating relationships between the Pentagon and its clients. It just seems like an obvious conflict of interest if he or his family members continue to profit from that business."

While Dodd advised defense startups on how to navigate the Pentagon, he simultaneously held senior government positions at the Defense Innovation Unit, or DIU. Dodd worked for DIU from at least 2022 until September 2025, when he was confirmed as assistant secretary of critical technologies, a position that helps steer the military's defense-industrial policy. The six defense-tech sectors that Dioltas [works](https://substack.com/redirect/32f0452c-7e0c-4276-b196-2c09cc5006ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in, including quantum technologies and microelectronics, overlap with sectors that Dodd's Pentagon office manages. If a contractor's work falls outside those sectors, Dioltas [advertises](https://substack.com/redirect/32f0452c-7e0c-4276-b196-2c09cc5006ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the ability to introduce it to "stakeholders defining future needs."
"The people who shape requirements and fund programs know us by name because we work alongside them," Dioltas's [website](https://substack.com/redirect/32f0452c-7e0c-4276-b196-2c09cc5006ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) boasts, one of at least a dozen references on the site to its ability to connect clients with government officials to help them earn contracts. Dioltas says it will stay "behind the scenes, where the work gets done" as it guides clients "through the moments where access means something."
Since Dodd's confirmation, Dioltas has made at least a dozen social-media posts promoting his official appearances at industry conferences that Dioltas also attended. It has described these events as [opportunities](https://substack.com/redirect/f5626d79-2fd6-41a6-9dbe-954e965ea98b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to [engage](https://substack.com/redirect/33867ab1-a7ef-4261-b26f-6ca526e96481?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with government leaders, and in one case it urged its followers to register for an event [hosted](https://substack.com/redirect/8844ceb8-9bfd-453b-88ab-0f70a20a7196?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Dodd's Pentagon office. The event, held in October, introduced the successor to a research contract managed by the Defense Technical Information Center, which reports to Dodd's office. Under the current version of the contract, ManTech, which Dioltas has previously listed as a client, won two awards worth up to around $542 million earlier this year. DTIC did not answer Drop Site's questions about whether Dodd's office was involved.
Wes Bryant, an Air Force special operations veteran who served as chief of the Pentagon's recently [shuttered](https://substack.com/redirect/4b57f6c2-8c0f-4c27-8bca-1763cd6640ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Civilian Protection Center, told Drop Site that Dioltas was "very clearly, without saying it, selling access directly to him right on their website."
Bryant previously worked in business development for defense contractors including L3Harris. A key objective of the work was developing relationships with Pentagon officials. He said that he was required to log each government contact he engaged and rate their value for influencing contract decisions.
Someone in Dodd's position would be deemed high value. "Those are the relationships that people out in industry salivate over," Bryant said.
Dodd has championed acquisition reform as a primary [means](https://substack.com/redirect/5694c2af-129e-4061-bb08-2c3e7de1446d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of accelerating the military's adoption of commercial technology. He has advocated the expansion of a [controversial](https://substack.com/redirect/c608352c-b8d8-48ba-a836-0ca01ae5ef12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) funding arrangement that fast-tracks the contracting process and [sidesteps](https://substack.com/redirect/b4c194e4-0401-4c95-8018-54f948a4905c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) federal acquisition regulations, known as "Other Transaction Authority" (OTA). As assistant secretary for critical technologies, Dodd works within the Office of Research and Engineering, which supervises department-wide prototyping of technology, much of which runs through OTAs.
"If I meet a non-traditional company that I'm interested in, I can get them on contract at the speed of business," Dodd said in an October [interview](https://substack.com/redirect/8b7e0e38-d501-4885-8979-6bc1d1720f34?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
William Hartung, an expert on Pentagon budgeting, described OTAs as lucrative long-term commitments with minimal oversight. "Dodd's promotion of OTAs could pad the bottom lines of Dioltas's clients," he told Drop Site.
Companies with ties to Dodd have received fast-tracked funding in technology areas he oversees. For example, SkyWater Technology, a Dioltas client and microelectronics manufacturer, received $30.9 million in OTA funding in June. Dodd gave a speech at a [SkyWater-hosted event](https://substack.com/redirect/fd09109a-169b-4484-915a-842119190af3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the following month and invests up to $15,000 in the firm, according to his disclosures. Allen Control Systems, a startup with no federal contracts in procurement records before Dodd took office, received two prototype OTAs worth at least $6.5 million earlier this year, which funded efforts to adapt its technology for the Army and the Marines. It then won an Army counter-drone contract [worth up](https://substack.com/redirect/0273f0bd-237f-4b1a-b778-20bd4c9de0e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to $500 million in September, and a few months later, in mid-November, it was selected to join a [Pentagon directed-energy](https://substack.com/redirect/77d01e29-3ae7-4cfc-a482-15730beb66ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) test program [designed](https://substack.com/redirect/e15c1fa8-d376-4e51-8c71-dad2b6a618ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to lead directly to funding. Dodd's office is a partner on this program.
Venture capitalists and contractors have pushed to expand the use of OTAs, as they[ give companies more leverage](https://substack.com/redirect/b4c194e4-0401-4c95-8018-54f948a4905c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over negotiations and reduce transparency and oversight. The Silicon Valley Defense Group celebrated the Trump administration's embrace of OTAs in its[ 2026 annual report](https://substack.com/redirect/c1974fa6-d0d7-4497-a8ed-02d1ce099d27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--which included Dodd's statement to investors and founders that "the Department's checkbook is open" for fast-moving firms.
In recent [interviews](https://substack.com/redirect/a0a5e2d9-db8a-4655-bada-901f2d3b53da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Dodd has explained that one way he gets firms on contract as fast as possible is by routing them through consortiums, or groups of companies. "That can be literally like same day stuff if we want to get a performer on contract," he told [Federal News Network](https://substack.com/redirect/d4523a72-97ac-4859-8120-41e394c6a8a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last month.
Around half of the Pentagon's [OTA spending](https://substack.com/redirect/c608352c-b8d8-48ba-a836-0ca01ae5ef12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is directed to consortiums. Federal records list the consortium as the recipient of a federal contract, and often do not show which individual firms were paid through it. The Government Accountability Office and the War Department's [Inspector General](https://substack.com/redirect/a486c87b-2362-4ed9-abdd-3a6a7154d9f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) have [repeatedly](https://substack.com/redirect/e4a2c220-540f-4cdc-ae3f-fede544a17f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) flagged weak oversight of these middlemen.
## "A Conflict on Steroids"
Dodd worked as an advisor to the National Security Technology Accelerator, or NSTXL, from August 2021 to June 2025. NSTXL is a nonprofit that manages consortia of defense companies and handles [billions](https://substack.com/redirect/d273025b-3c5c-4b83-b650-0bd51a2e1f90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Pentagon contracts, including a Space Force OTA worth up to [$12.1 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/96272389-deb5-407d-ba92-825ccdc83135?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). NSTXL [now manages](https://substack.com/redirect/9f7d46ad-7212-4a54-9e9f-3572c7926163?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) OTA contracts for Dodd's[ department](https://substack.com/redirect/c1ade4d8-4bce-40ea-818d-a58147432de1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including a new[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/64b37c45-86b8-4892-b3fb-591fc7bd33b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)OTA related to energy weapons worth up to [$500 million](https://substack.com/redirect/64b37c45-86b8-4892-b3fb-591fc7bd33b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Another OTA it manages, which is used across the Pentagon's research and engineering office, has handled more than $3 billion in awards, according to [NSTXL](https://substack.com/redirect/a774e3d4-a7c1-4d64-8370-d975e2e50585?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Dodd's Pentagon microelectronics program, the Microelectronics Commons, is among the projects that run through it. Dodd [delivered](https://substack.com/redirect/03b3f5e5-6b84-436a-881c-1c031e1f7c36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Pentagon's leadership keynote at the Microelectronics Commons annual meeting in February, an event organized by NSTXL, where Dioltas said it [spent the week](https://substack.com/redirect/b7c8251b-69fb-485d-a993-20306c4cd23c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "engaging with our portfolio companies, industry partners, and Department of War leadership."
Drop Site reviewed more than $100 million worth of recent OTAs to NSTXL that do not detail which member firms were paid. NSTXL does not list its members publicly, and according to its [tax filings](https://substack.com/redirect/bd59d2b4-7e15-49f9-9504-92a0b4501209?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), it has no written policy for document retention, whistleblowers, and conflicts of interest.
NSTXL reported over $10 million in losses in its two most recent tax filings for [2023](https://substack.com/redirect/447d80ee-26b8-46c4-a20e-5c053a524e75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [2024](https://substack.com/redirect/d7aaf005-c210-4a51-b199-255650322fc3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Over the same period, it transferred over $10 million more than its entire revenue to a for-profit firm owned by its founder.
NSTXL reported $66.9 million in revenue over 2023 and 2024--mostly from government fees--but paid its contract consultant Innovas a total of $77.3 million over the same period. Tim Greeff, the founder and president of NSTXL, is also CEO and majority owner of Innovas, according to the filings.
Dodd reported $303,000 in income and bonus fees from Innovas in both of his disclosures.
NSTXL and Innovas did not respond to Drop Site's inquiries.
Hartung called NSTXL's relationship with Dodd "a conflict on steroids," adding that "Congress should force disclosure of companies NSTXL funnels money to and look more closely at Dodd's role in brokering and possibly profiting from these arrangements."
